explanation_english: “趨” can mean to hurry toward or to head for something; it also indicates tendency or inclination toward a state or direction. It commonly appears in compounds (e.g. 'trend', 'tendency') and idioms (e.g. 'flock to').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 市場有趨勢，大家要留意投資風險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si5 coeng4 jau5 ceoi1 si3, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 lau4 ji3 tau4 zi1 fung1 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市场有趋势，大家要留意投资风险。
examples.english_sentence: The market has a trend; everyone should pay attention to investment risks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新開嘅餐廳一開幕就被人趨之若鶩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 hoi1 ge3 caan1 teng1 jat1 hoi1 muk6 zau6 bei6 jan4 ceoi1 zi1 joek6 nguk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新开的餐厅一开业就被人趋之若鹜。
examples.english_sentence: The newly opened restaurant was immediately swarmed by people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢趨向採取比較保守嘅做法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ceoi1 hoeng3 coi2 ceoi2 bei2 gaau3 bou2 sau2 ge3 zou6 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他趋向采取比较保守的做法。
examples.english_sentence: He tends to adopt a relatively conservative approach.

mandarin_meaning: 趋之若鹜：形容许多人像鸭子一样蜂拥而至，争相前往。
english_meaning: To flock to something like ducks; to swarm to or rush toward something in large numbers.
explanation_mandarin: 形容许多人像鸭子一样蜂拥而至，争相前往。常用于描述对某事物、活动或场所大量涌入或追捧的情形。
explanation_english: Describes many people flocking to a place or event like ducks; used to indicate a large, eager crowd rushing toward or clamoring for something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新開張嗰間商場一開業，市民就趨之若鶩，個場面好熱鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 hoi1 zoeng1 go2 gaan1 soeng1 coeng4 jat1 hoi1 jip6, si5 man4 zau6 ceoi1 zi1 joek6 muk6, go3 coeng4 min6 hou2 jit6 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新开业的商场一开张，市民就蜂拥而至，场面很热闹。
examples.english_sentence: When the newly opened mall opened, people flocked to it, and the scene was very lively.

mandarin_meaning: 趋利避害 (qū lì bì hài) — 追求利益，回避危害或损失
english_meaning: To seek benefits and avoid harms; to act out of self-interest or opportunistically
explanation_mandarin: 形容为追求利益而回避危险或损失，常带有功利或投机的含义。
explanation_english: Describes behavior of pursuing benefits while avoiding risks or harms; often implies self-interested or opportunistic motives.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢淨係趨利避害，唔顧及同事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 zing6 hai6 ceoi1 lei6 bei6 hoi6, m4 gu3 kap6 tung4 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事只会趋利避害，不顾同事。
examples.english_sentence: He only looks out for his own benefit and avoids risks, ignoring his colleagues.

mandarin_meaning: 趋势
english_meaning: trend; tendency; direction of development
explanation_mandarin: 指事物發展或變化的方向和傾向，常用來描述市場、經濟、社會等整體的動向。
explanation_english: Refers to the direction or tendency of how something develops or changes; commonly used to describe overall movements in markets, economics, society, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家市場嘅趨勢係向網上購物發展。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 si5 coeng4 ge3 ceoi1 si3 hai6 hoeng3 mong5 soeng6 gau3 mat6 faat3 zin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在市場的趨勢是向網上購物發展。
examples.english_sentence: The current market trend is moving toward online shopping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 投資者要留意經濟趨勢，唔好只睇短期波動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 zi1 ze2 jiu3 lau4 ji3 ging1 zai3 ceoi1 si3, m4 hou2 zi2 tai2 dyun2 kei4 bo1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 投資者要留意經濟趨勢，不要只看短期波動。
examples.english_sentence: Investors should pay attention to economic trends, not just short-term fluctuations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢種趨勢好難逆轉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zung2 ceoi1 si3 hou2 naan4 jik6 zyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這種趨勢很難逆轉。
examples.english_sentence: This kind of trend is hard to reverse.

mandarin_meaning: 趋吉避凶（趋向吉祥，避开不吉利或灾祸）
english_meaning: Seek good fortune and avoid misfortune; pursue auspiciousness and stay away from disaster.
explanation_mandarin: 表示追求吉利、避免不祥或灾祸，常用來形容人們為保平安而採取的避險或趨利行為。
explanation_english: Describes pursuing auspicious outcomes and avoiding misfortune; often used to characterize actions people take to stay safe or obtain favorable outcomes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農曆新年大家都會拜神，希望趨吉避凶，求個好運。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 lik6 san1 nin4 daai6 gaa1 dou1 wui5 baai3 san4, hei1 mong6 ceoi1 gat1 bei6 hung1, kau4 go3 hou2 wan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 农历新年大家都会拜神，希望趋吉避凶，求个好运。
examples.english_sentence: During Lunar New Year, everyone prays to the gods hoping to seek good fortune and avoid misfortune, asking for good luck.

mandarin_meaning: 趋向（趋于、倾向）
english_meaning: to tend toward; to incline; trend; tendency
explanation_mandarin: 表示朝某一方向發展或具有某種傾向；也可作名詞表示趨勢或傾向性。
explanation_english: Indicates moving toward or having an inclination; can also be used as a noun to mean a trend or tendency.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家好多人趨向喺網上買嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 hou2 do1 jan4 ceoi1 hoeng3 hai2 mong5 soeng6 maai5 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在很多人趨向在網上購物。
examples.english_sentence: Nowadays many people tend to shop online.

mandarin_meaning: 趋炎附势（qū yán fù shì）：指依附有權勢者，諂媚巴結以謀取利益。
english_meaning: To curry favor with the powerful; to ingratiate oneself with those in power for personal gain.
explanation_mandarin: 形容有人見到有權勢或有利可圖的一方，便逢迎諂媚、依附巴結以圖好處。
explanation_english: Describes someone who flatters and attaches themselves to people in power to gain advantage or favor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日趨炎附勢，見到有權勢嘅人就向佢靠攏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 cau1 jim4 fu6 sai3, gin3 dou3 jau5 kyun4 sai3 ge3 jan4 zau6 hoeng3 keoi5 kaau3 lung5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是趋炎附势，见到有权势的人就向他们靠拢。
examples.english_sentence: He always curries favor with the powerful; whenever he sees someone influential he moves to align himself with them.

mandarin_meaning: （文言）跳躍；躍起
english_meaning: to leap; to spring up; to bound (archaic/literary)
explanation_mandarin: 趯為文言字，意指跳躍、躍起，現代漢語中較少使用，常見於古文或書面語中。
explanation_english: An archaic/literary verb meaning to leap or spring up. Rarely used in modern spoken Chinese and mainly found in classical or literary contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 馬兒奮力趯起，衝過低矮嘅石欄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa5 ji4 fan5 lik6 tik1 hei2, cung1 gwo3 dai1 ngai2 ge3 sek6 laan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 馬兒奮力一躍，衝過低矮的石欄。
examples.english_sentence: The horse leaped powerfully, clearing the low stone railing.

mandarin_meaning: 逃走的人；胆小或逃避责任的人（口语、贬义）
english_meaning: a person who runs away; a coward or shirker (colloquial, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「趯佬」是廣東話口語俚語，用來形容遇事逃避、溜走或不敢面對問題的人，帶有貶義。常用於責備或嘲諷對方。
explanation_english: “趯佬” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe someone who runs away, shirks responsibility, or is cowardly when facing problems. It is derogatory and often used to scold or mock.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做趯佬，有咩問題一齊面對啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 tit3 lou2, jau5 me1 man6 tai4 jat1 cai4 min6 deoi3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要做趯佬，有什麼問題一起面對吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a 'tit lou' — if there's a problem, let's face it together.

mandarin_meaning: 夜間外出遊蕩、鬼祟出門
english_meaning: to wander/prowl about at night; to go out at night (often sneaking or causing trouble)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，指在夜間外出遊蕩或鬼祟出門，常帶有不安全或惹事的含義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term meaning to go out roaming or prowling at night, often with a sense of sneaking around or engaging in risky/mischievous behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽叫佢唔好半夜趯更出街，話好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 giu3 keoi5 m4 hou2 bun3 je6 tit3 gang1 ceot1 gaai1, waa6 hou2 ngoi4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽叫他不要半夜趯更出門，說很危險。
examples.english_sentence: Mom told him not to go prowling around at night – it's dangerous.

mandarin_meaning: 逃走；溜走；走佬（粤语俚语）
english_meaning: to run away; to scram; to leave abruptly (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: “趯路”是粵語口語/俚語，表示迅速離開或逃跑，常用於香港非正式語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to run away or leave abruptly. Common in informal Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到警察即刻趯路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou2 ging2 caat3 zik1 hak1 teot3 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到警察馬上逃走。
examples.english_sentence: He saw the police and immediately ran away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 附近有事唔安全，最好趯路唔好逗留。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fu6 gan6 jau5 si6 m4 on1 cyun4, zeoi3 hou2 teot3 lou6 m4 hou2 dau6 lau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 附近有危險，最好逃走不要逗留。
examples.english_sentence: There's danger nearby; it's best to get out of there and not linger.

mandarin_meaning: 赶、催促；匆忙走动
english_meaning: to hurry; to rush; to urge someone to move quickly
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用字，表示催促、趕緊或匆忙走動，常用於口語表達「快點趲」之類的句子。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to hurry or rush (to urge someone to move quickly). Often used in spoken phrases like “hurry up.”

examples.cantonese_sentence: 快啲趲啦，我哋遲到啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faai3 di1 zaan2 laa1, ngo5 dei6 ci4 dou3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 快点赶吧，我们要迟到了。
examples.english_sentence: Hurry up, we're going to be late.

mandarin_meaning: 足（zú；足够/足部/足足 等）
english_meaning: foot; sufficient/enough; (emphatic) full/entire
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞 / 形容詞 / 副詞
explanation_mandarin: 「足」可作名詞指腳或足部；也可作形容詞/副詞，表示足夠、充足或強調數量或程度（常見於複合詞如「足夠」、重疊「足足」、或用於「足有」表示達到某數量）。
explanation_english: “足” can be a noun meaning the foot or foot area; it can also be an adjective/adverb meaning sufficient/adequate or used emphatically to indicate a full amount or degree (common in compounds like 足夠, reduplication 足足, or constructions like 足有 meaning 'as many as').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話佢足部需要做物理治療。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 keoi5 zuk1 bou6 seoi1 jiu3 zou6 mat6 lei5 zi6 liu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 医生说他的足部需要做物理治疗。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said his foot needs physiotherapy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢足足等咗兩個鐘先到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zuk1 zuk1 dang2 zo2 loeng5 go3 zung1 sin1 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他足足等了两个小时才到。
examples.english_sentence: He waited a full two hours before arriving.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲食物足夠俾大家食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 sik6 mat6 zuk1 gau3 bei2 daai6 gaa1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些食物足够大家吃。
examples.english_sentence: This food is enough for everyone.

mandarin_meaning: 足不出户（不出門、長時間呆在家裡）
english_meaning: to stay at home; not to step outside the door; confined at home
explanation_mandarin: 表達長時間不出門、待在家裡不外出的狀態，可描述習慣性不出門或因特殊原因（如生病、封城）而留在家中。
explanation_english: Describes the state of not leaving one's home for a long time. Can refer to a habitual tendency to stay indoors or to staying home due to special circumstances (e.g., illness, lockdown).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都足不出戶，唔鍾意同人接觸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6, m4 zung1 ji3 tung4 jan4 zip3 zuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天都足不出户，不喜歡和人接觸。
examples.english_sentence: He stays at home all the time and doesn't like to have contact with people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 疫情期間，政府呼籲大家盡量足不出戶，減低傳染風險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jik6 cing4 kei4 gaan1, zing3 fu2 fu1 jyu6 daai6 gaa1 zeon6 loeng6 zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6, gaam2 dai1 cyun4 jim5 fung1 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 疫情期間，政府呼籲大家盡量足不出戶，降低傳播風險。
examples.english_sentence: During the epidemic, the government urged everyone to stay at home as much as possible to reduce the risk of transmission.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為行動不便，已經足不出戶好耐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 hang4 dung6 bat1 bin6, ji5 ging1 zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6 hou2 noi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因為行動不便，已經很久都足不出戶。
examples.english_sentence: Because he has mobility issues, he has been confined at home for a long time.

mandarin_meaning: 足不出户
english_meaning: to stay indoors; not to leave the house
explanation_mandarin: 表示整天待在家里不外出，常用于形容因天气、疾病或防疫措施等而不出门的情况。
explanation_english: A phrase meaning to remain at home and not go outside, often used to describe staying indoors due to weather, illness, quarantine, or other reasons.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 由於落大雨，我今日決定足不出戶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau4 jyu1 lok6 daai6 jyu5, ngo5 gam1 jat6 kyut3 ding6 zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 由于下大雨，我今天决定足不出户。
examples.english_sentence: Because of the heavy rain, I've decided not to leave the house today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 疫情期間長期足不出戶會影響身心健康。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jik6 cing4 kei4 gaan1 coeng4 kei4 zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6 wui5 jing2 hoeng2 san1 sam1 gin6 hong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 疫情期间长期足不出户会影响身心健康。
examples.english_sentence: Prolonged staying indoors during the pandemic can affect physical and mental health.

mandarin_meaning: 足不出户（不外出，待在家里）
english_meaning: to stay at home; not leave one's house; housebound
explanation_mandarin: 形容長時間待在家裡、不外出。可用於字面意思（如生病或居家隔離）或比喻（如長期不社交）。
explanation_english: Describes staying at home and not going out. Can be used literally (e.g., due to illness or quarantine) or figuratively (e.g., long-term withdrawal from social life).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢病咗幾個月，足不出戶，好少見人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 beng6 zo2 gei2 go3 jyut6, zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6, hou2 siu2 gin3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他病了几个月，足不出户，很少见人。
examples.english_sentence: He was ill for several months and didn't leave the house; he was rarely seen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 疫情期間，政府建議大家足不出戶，盡量留喺屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jing4 cing4 kei4 gaan1, zing3 fu2 gin3 ji5 daai6 gaa1, zuk1 bat1 ceot1 wu6, zeon6 loeng6 lau4 hai2 uk1 kei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 疫情期间，政府建议大家足不出户，尽量待在家里。
examples.english_sentence: During the epidemic, the government advised everyone to stay at home as much as possible.

mandarin_meaning: 足以（足够，可以）
english_meaning: to be sufficient; enough to
explanation_mandarin: 表示某種條件、原因或程度已經達到，可以產生預期的結果或效果，常用於書面語或正式語境。
explanation_english: Indicates that a condition, reason, or degree is sufficient to produce a desired result; commonly used in formal or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個理由足以令我改變主意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 lei5 jau4 zuk1 ji5 ling6 ngo5 goi2 bin3 zyu2 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个理由足以让我改变主意。
examples.english_sentence: This reason is enough to make me change my mind.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢已經有足以應付考試嘅準備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 ging1 jau5 zuk1 ji5 jing3 fu6 haau2 si3 ge3 zeon2 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他已经有足以应付考试的准备。
examples.english_sentence: He already has enough preparation to cope with the exam.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 晚餐份量足以餵飽兩個人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maan5 caan1 fan6 loeng6 zuk1 ji5 wai3 baau2 loeng5 go3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚餐的份量足以喂饱两个人。
examples.english_sentence: The dinner portion is enough to feed two people.

mandarin_meaning: 足夠 (zúgòu)
english_meaning: enough; sufficient
explanation_mandarin: 表示數量或程度足以滿足需要或達到要求。
explanation_english: Indicates that the quantity or degree is sufficient to meet a need or requirement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲食物已經足夠我哋食喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 sik6 mat6 ji5 ging1 zuk1 gau3 ngo5 dei6 sik6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些食物已經足夠我們吃了。
examples.english_sentence: These foods are already enough for us to eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢冇足夠嘅時間準備考試。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou5 zuk1 gau3 ge3 si4 gaan3 zeon2 bei6 haau2 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他沒有足夠的時間準備考試。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't have enough time to prepare for the exam.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個房間面積足夠三個人住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 fong4 gaan1 min6 zik1 zuk1 gau3 saam1 go3 jan4 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個房間面積足夠三個人住。
examples.english_sentence: The room is big enough for three people to live in.

mandarin_meaning: 足字旁（字的偏旁部首，表示與腳、行動有關的字）
english_meaning: the 'foot' radical (a character component indicating feet or actions/movement)
explanation_mandarin: 指漢字裡的「足」部首（足字旁），常見於表示腳、走路或動作的字，如「跑」、「踢」。
explanation_english: Refers to the 'foot' radical (足) used as a component in Chinese characters. It often appears in characters related to feet, movement, or actions (e.g., 跑, 踢).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字有足字邊，好似「跑」、「踢」嗰啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 jau5 zuk1 zi6 bin1, hou2 ci5 'paau2', 'tek3' go2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字有足字旁，比如“跑”、“踢”等。
examples.english_sentence: This character has the 'foot' radical, like '跑' and '踢'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學中文字時，要留意邊啲字係有足字邊，通常同行為或動作有關。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 zung1 man4 zi6 si4, jiu3 lau4 ji3 bin1 di1 zi6 hai6 jau5 zuk1 zi6 bin1, tung1 soeng4 tung4 hang4 wai6 wo6 dung6 zok3 jau5 gwaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学汉字时，要注意哪些字有足字旁，通常与行为或动作有关。
examples.english_sentence: When learning Chinese characters, pay attention to which ones have the 'foot' radical — they are often related to actions or movement.

mandarin_meaning: 料足 / 內容豐富 / 很有料
english_meaning: full of ingredients; substantial; content‑rich; juicy (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示食物材料多、分量足，或指節目、新聞、八卦等內容豐富、有看頭、有料可談。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression meaning abundant in ingredients or substantial in content. Used for food that is generously made, or for programs/news/gossip that are rich, interesting, or full of material.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碗湯真係足料，入面有好多材料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wun2 tong1 zan1 hai6 zuk1 liu6, jap6 min6 jau5 hou2 do1 coi4 liu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这碗汤真的很足料，里面有很多材料。
examples.english_sentence: This bowl of soup is really full of ingredients; there's a lot in it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢段八卦真係好足料，講到啲明星嘅秘密。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dyun6 baat3 gwaa3 zan1 hai6 hou2 zuk1 liu6, gong2 dou3 di1 ming4 sing1 ge3 bei6 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这段八卦真的很有料，讲到了明星的秘密。
examples.english_sentence: This gossip is really juicy; it reveals the celebrities' secrets.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個節目好足料，資料同訪問都好豐富。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zit3 muk6 hou2 zuk1 liu6, zi1 liu2 tung4 fong2 man6 dou1 hou2 fung1 fu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个节目很有料，资料和采访都很丰富。
examples.english_sentence: This program is very substantial; the information and interviews are quite rich.

mandarin_meaning: 足智多謀（zú zhì duō móu）：形容人非常有智慧、善於出主意和策劃。
english_meaning: Resourceful; full of wisdom and strategy — describes someone clever at devising plans and solutions.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人很有智慧且善於籌劃、想出解決問題的方法或策略。
explanation_english: Describes a person who is intelligent and highly resourceful, adept at coming up with plans and solutions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係足智多謀，成日都諗到好辦法幫公司度過難關。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 zuk1 zi3 do1 mau4, sing4 jat6 dou1 nam2 dou3 hou2 baan6 faat3 bong1 gung1 si1 dou6 gwo3 naan4 gwaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是足智多謀，經常想出好辦法幫公司度過難關。
examples.english_sentence: He is truly resourceful; he often comes up with good solutions to help the company through difficult times.

mandarin_meaning: 足月（足月出生）
english_meaning: full-term (baby/pregnancy)
explanation_mandarin: 指懷孕達到足夠的妊娠週數（通常為37至42週）而出生，或用來形容胎兒/嬰兒成熟、發育正常。
explanation_english: Refers to a pregnancy that reaches full term (typically 37–42 weeks) or to a baby born at full term; used to describe an infant who is mature and has normal development.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽話BB係足月出世，唔使太擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 waa6 BB hai6 zuk1 jyut6 ceot1 sai3, m4 sai2 taai3 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽說寶寶是足月出生，不用太擔心。
examples.english_sentence: Mom said the baby was born full-term, so don't worry too much.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生檢查之後話嬰兒係足月，生長情況良好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 gim2 caa4 zi1 hau6 waa6 jing1 ji4 hai6 zuk1 jyut6, saang1 zoeng2 cing4 fong3 loeng4 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 醫生檢查後說嬰兒是足月，生長情況良好。
examples.english_sentence: After the examination, the doctor said the infant was full-term and growing well.

mandarin_meaning: 完整版；完整無刪節
english_meaning: full version; complete/unabridged edition; in full
explanation_mandarin: 指資料或作品未經刪節或刪減，保留全部原始內容的版本，也可用來表示「足額、全數」。
explanation_english: Refers to an edition/version of a work that is unabridged and retains all original content; can also mean 'in full' or 'the full amount'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本書係足本，冇刪節。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 syu1 hai6 zuk1 bun2, mou5 saan1 zit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這本書是足本，沒有刪節。
examples.english_sentence: This book is the full (unabridged) edition; nothing has been omitted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋已經付足本，唔使再交錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 ji5 ging1 fu6 zuk1 bun2, m4 sai2 zoi3 gaau1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們已經付足本，不需要再付錢。
examples.english_sentence: They have already paid the full amount; there's no need to pay more.

mandarin_meaning: 足球 (zúqiú)
english_meaning: football; soccer
explanation_mandarin: 一种以脚踢球为主的团队运动，也可指该运动使用的球。
explanation_english: A team sport primarily played by kicking a ball with the feet; can also refer to the ball used in the sport.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚去睇足球比賽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 heoi3 tai2 zuk1 kau4 bei2 coi3
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚去看足球比赛。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to watch a football (soccer) match tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成日喺公園踢足球。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 sing4 jat6 hai2 gung1 jyun4 tek3 zuk1 kau4
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们经常在公园踢足球。
examples.english_sentence: They often play football in the park.

mandarin_meaning: 足球场
english_meaning: football (soccer) field; football stadium; soccer pitch
explanation_mandarin: 指進行足球運動或舉辦足球比賽的場地，通常有草地或人造草皮以及看台與場邊設施。
explanation_english: A venue where football (soccer) is played or matches are held; typically has grass or artificial turf, spectator stands, and related facilities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋下個禮拜去足球場睇波。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 heoi3 zuk1 kau4 coeng4 tai2 bo1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们下个礼拜去足球场看球。
examples.english_sentence: We're going to the football stadium next week to watch a match.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 足球場今晚有一場比賽，記得早啲去搶位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zuk1 kau4 coeng4 gam1 maan5 jau5 jat1 coeng4 bei2 coi3, gei3 dak1 zou2 di1 heoi3 coeng2 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 足球场今晚有一场比赛，记得早点去占位置。
examples.english_sentence: There's a match at the football stadium tonight — remember to get there early to secure seats.

mandarin_meaning: 称重足/足量；可靠、货真价实（粤语俚语）
english_meaning: gives full weight / honest weight; reliable, genuine, worth the money (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面上指秤出來的重量足夠、不會少給，延伸為人或物可靠、貨真價實、不會欺騙顧客或誇大其實。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term literally meaning 'full weight' — originally used to say the measured weight is correct and you aren't being shortchanged. Figuratively it describes something or someone as reliable, genuine, substantial, or worth the price.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間肉舖好足秤，秤得夠，唔會短斤少兩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 juk6 pou3 hou2 zuk1 cang3, cang3 dak1 gau3, m4 wui5 dyun2 gan1 siu2 loeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家肉铺称得足，不会短斤少两。
examples.english_sentence: This butcher shop gives full weight — they weigh properly and won't shortchange you.

mandarin_meaning: 足球總會（足球管理機構）
english_meaning: football association (governing body for football)
explanation_mandarin: 「足總」是「足球總會」的簡稱，指負責管理、組織和安排足球賽事與相關事務的機構，例如香港足總或中國足總。
explanation_english: A colloquial abbreviation of "football association" — the organization responsible for managing, organizing, and arranging football competitions and related affairs (e.g., the Hong Kong FA).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港足總公佈咗今季賽程。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 zuk1 zung2 gung1 bou3 zo2 gam1 gwai3 coi3 cing4
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港足总公布了本赛季的赛程。
examples.english_sentence: The Hong Kong Football Association announced the schedule for this season.

mandarin_meaning: 足以看出；可見
english_meaning: it shows; it is evident that; clearly indicates
explanation_mandarin: 用於表示能從某事或現象中看出某種情況或特徵，相當於「足以看出」或「可見」，多用於書面語或正式語境。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something clearly shows or proves a certain situation or characteristic; equivalent to 'it is evident that' or 'this shows that'. Common in formal or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遲到咁多次，足見佢唔重視呢份工作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci4 dou3 gam3 do1 ci3, zuk1 gin3 keoi5 m4 zung6 si6 ni1 fan6 gung1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他迟到这么多次，足以看出他不重视这份工作。
examples.english_sentence: He's been late so many times; it shows that he doesn't take this job seriously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司嘅決策失誤，足見管理層需要作出改革。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ge3 kyut3 caak3 sat1 ng6, zuk1 gin3 gun2 lei5 cang4 seoi1 jiu3 zok3 ceot1 goi2 gaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的决策失误，足以看出管理层需要进行改革。
examples.english_sentence: The company's flawed decision-making shows that the management needs to make reforms.

mandarin_meaning: 足足；整整（表示數量、時間等多得足夠或達到整數）
english_meaning: a full; as much as; a whole (used to emphasize amount or duration)
explanation_mandarin: 用作副詞，強調數量或時間達到整數或比預期多，如「足足兩個小時」表示整整兩個小時，很長的時間。
explanation_english: Used as an adverb to emphasize an amount or duration being whole or surprisingly large (e.g., "a full two hours").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我等咗佢足足兩個鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dang2 zo2 keoi5 zuk1 zuk1 loeng5 go3 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我等了他足足兩個小時。
examples.english_sentence: I waited for him a full two hours.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢足足食咗三碗飯先停。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zuk1 zuk1 sik6 zo2 saam1 wun2 faan6 sin1 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他足足吃了三碗飯才停。
examples.english_sentence: He ate as many as three bowls of rice before stopping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份報告足足有五十頁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 zuk1 zuk1 jau5 ng5 sap6 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份報告足足有五十頁。
examples.english_sentence: This report has as many as fifty pages.

mandarin_meaning: 足迹 (zújì)：脚印、痕迹；（也指）行踪
english_meaning: footprints; tracks; traces of someone's presence or activities
explanation_mandarin: 指人或動物行走後留下的腳印，也可引申為某人行動或活動留下的痕跡或行蹤。
explanation_english: Refers to footprints left by people or animals; can also be used figuratively for traces or records of someone's movements or activities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺沙灘上見到一串足跡，估計係隻狗嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 saa1 taan1 soeng6 gin3 dou2 jat1 cyun4 zuk1 zek3, gu2 gai3 hai6 zek3 gau2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在沙滩上看到一串足迹，估计是一只狗留下的。
examples.english_sentence: I saw a line of footprints on the beach; I guess they were left by a dog.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警察追查嫌疑犯嘅足跡，想知道佢去過邊度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 caat3 zeoi1 caa4 jim4 ji4 faan6 ge3 zuk1 zek3, soeng2 zi1 dou3 keoi5 heoi3 gwo3 bin1 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方在追查嫌疑犯的足迹，想知道他去過哪里。
examples.english_sentence: The police are tracing the suspect's movements to find out where he has been.

mandarin_meaning: 足金（純金，通常指24K純度較高的黃金）
english_meaning: pure gold (typically 24K gold)
explanation_mandarin: 指純度較高、通常為24K的黃金，常見於珠寶或金飾，含金量高但金屬較柔軟，佩戴或加工時需注意保護。
explanation_english: Refers to high-purity gold, typically 24K. Commonly used for jewelry and gold ornaments; it has a high gold content and is relatively soft, so it requires care when worn or worked.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢枚戒指係足金做嘅，價錢幾貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 mui4 gaai3 zi2 hai6 zuk1 gam1 zou6 ge3, gaa3 cin2 gei2 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這枚戒指是足金做的，價錢很貴。
examples.english_sentence: This ring is made of pure gold; it's quite expensive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 婚禮上，新娘戴住足金手鐲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fan1 lai5 soeng6, san1 noeng4 daai3 zyu6 zuk1 gam1 sau2 zoek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在婚禮上，新娘戴著足金手鐲。
examples.english_sentence: At the wedding, the bride wore a pure gold bracelet.

mandarin_meaning: 趴（趴着）——俯卧、伏在某处；口语中也可表示趴下、倒下或疲倦想睡
english_meaning: to lie face down; to sprawl or flop down; colloquially to slump or crash (from tiredness)
explanation_mandarin: 「趴」用來表示人或動物俯臥、趴着，例如「趴喺床上」。在口語中亦可用作「趴下/趴低」，形容倒下或疲倦想睡。
explanation_english: Used to indicate a person or animal lying prone or face-down (e.g., 'lying on the bed'). In colloquial speech it can also mean to flop down or to slump/sleep from exhaustion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿仔趴喺地下，唔肯郁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 zai2 paa1 hai2 dei6 haa6, m4 hang2 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩趴在地上，不肯动。
examples.english_sentence: The child is lying sprawled on the floor and won't move.

mandarin_meaning: 趴下；蹲低；保持低調、隱藏行動
english_meaning: to lie face down or crouch low; to duck/keep a low profile (lay low)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示身體向下趴或蹲以避開危險或隱藏自己；亦可引申為在一段時間內低調、避風頭。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to lie or crouch down (to avoid danger or take cover); can also be used figuratively to mean staying low-profile or laying low for a period.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有嘢跌落嚟，快啲趴低！
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 je5 dit3 lok6 lai4, faai3 di1 paa1 dai1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有東西要掉下來，快趴下！
examples.english_sentence: Something's falling — get down/duck!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢上次捲入醜聞之後，一直趴低，冇公開露面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng5 ci3 gyun2 jap6 cau2 man4 zi1 hau6, jat1 zik6 paa1 dai1, mou5 gung1 hoi1 lou6 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上次捲入醜聞之後，一直保持低調，沒有公開露面。
examples.english_sentence: After being involved in the scandal, he laid low and didn't appear publicly.

mandarin_meaning: 趴在街上；比喻被打倒、慘敗或遭受羞辱（俚語，亦可作粗口）
english_meaning: to lie face-down on the street; figuratively, to be knocked down, utterly defeated, or humiliated (slang, can be vulgar)
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，字面指趴在街上，常用來形容被打倒、慘敗或當場倒下，也可作粗口罵人或表達侮辱意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb literally meaning to lie face-down on the street. It is often used to describe being knocked down, suffering a crushing defeat, or being humiliated. It can also be used as a vulgar insult.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀對手一拳打中，頓時趴街咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 deoi3 sau2 jat1 kyun4 daa2 zung3, deon6 si4 paa1 gaai1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被對手一拳打中，當場趴在地上。
examples.english_sentence: He got hit by his opponent's punch and fell flat on the ground.

mandarin_meaning: 跺（脚）；用力踏
english_meaning: to stamp/stomp (one's foot); to trample
explanation_mandarin: 趷常用於粵語口語，表示用腳用力跺或猛踏，有時帶有生氣、抗議或不耐煩的情緒色彩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese verb meaning to stamp or stomp the foot forcefully. It is often used colloquially and can convey anger, protest, or impatience.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嬲到喺度趷腳，大家都唔敢上前。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 nau1 dou3 hai2 dou6 hot3 goek3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 gam2 soeng5 cin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他气得在那儿跺脚，大家都不敢上前。
examples.english_sentence: He was so angry he was stomping his feet; everyone was afraid to approach.

mandarin_meaning: 讓一讓、讓開
english_meaning: move aside; get out of the way; scoot over
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，用來催促別人讓路或讓開位置，語氣可隨情境而禮貌或急促。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to urge someone to move aside or make room; can function as an interjection or verb and vary in politeness depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你趷下趷下啦，畀個位我過下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hot3 haa6 hot3 haa6 laa1, bei2 go3 wai2 ngo5 gwo3 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你讓一讓啦，讓我過一下路。
examples.english_sentence: Move aside, give me some room to get by.

mandarin_meaning: 支支吾吾、吞吞吐吐、結巴
english_meaning: to stammer; to speak hesitantly or incoherently; to be tongue-tied
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容說話結結巴巴、支支吾吾、吞吞吐吐，常因緊張、害怕或一時想不到合適說法而表現出來。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase describing speaking hesitantly or incoherently — stammering or being tongue-tied, often due to nervousness, embarrassment, or not knowing how to respond.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 畀老細問到啲數，佢即刻趷口趷舌，答唔到問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 lou5 sai3 man6 dou3 di1 sou3, keoi5 zik1 hak1 hot3 hau2 hot3 sit3, daap3 m4 dou2 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 被老闆問到一些數字時，他立刻支支吾吾，回答不出問題。
examples.english_sentence: When the boss asked him about the numbers, he immediately stammered and couldn't answer the questions.

mandarin_meaning: （被嚇得）跳起來；驚得抬腳
english_meaning: to jump/jerk (often from fright); to startle and lift a foot
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，通常指因驚嚇或受刺激而突然跳起或抬腳，常用於描寫被嚇到的反應。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to jump or jerk (often lifting a foot) usually from surprise or fright; describes a startled physical reaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個爆炸聲嚇到我趷腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 baau3 zaa3 seng1 haak3 dou3 ngo5 hot3 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 爆炸聲把我嚇得跳起來。
examples.english_sentence: The bang/explosion scared me and I jumped.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到老鼠即刻趷腳走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 lou5 syu2 zik1 haak1 hot3 goek3 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到老鼠立刻跳開走了。
examples.english_sentence: He saw a rat and immediately jumped away.

cantonese: 趷起條尾就知你屙屎定屙尿
jyutping: kut3 hei2 tiu4 mei5 zau6 zi1 nei5 o1 si2 ding6 o1 niu6
mandarin_meaning: 掀起（尾巴/褲子）就知道你是拉屎還是撒尿（用來比喻事情很明顯，一看就知道）
english_meaning: Lift up your tail and you'll know whether you shit or pee (used figuratively to say something is obvious)
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句粗俗的粵語俚語，字面上指掀起尾部就能分辨是大便還是小便，常用來表示某件事非常明顯、一看就知道真相。
explanation_english: A coarse Cantonese slang phrase. Literally means 'lift up the tail and you can tell if it's feces or urine.' It's used figuratively to say that something is so obvious you can tell immediately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話冇偷嘢？睇吓啲證據，趷起條尾就知你屙屎定屙尿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 mou5 tau1 je5? tai2 haa5 di1 zing3 geoi3, kut3 hei2 tiu4 mei5 zau6 zi1 nei5 o1 si2 ding6 o1 niu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說沒偷東西？看看證據，掀起尾巴就知道你是拉屎還是撒尿。
examples.english_sentence: You say you didn't steal anything? Look at the evidence — lift up your tail and you'll know whether you shit or pee.

mandarin_meaning: 一瘸一拐；走路不穩
english_meaning: limping; hobbling; walking unsteadily with a limp
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，形容走路一瘸一拐或步伐不穩，常用來描述人因腳痛或受傷而行走不便的狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone walking with a limp or unsteadily (hobbling), often because of pain or an injury to the leg/foot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日趷跛跛咁行路，可能係隻腳痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hot3 bat1 bat1 gam2 hang4 lou6, ho2 nang4 hai6 zek3 goek3 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是跛跛地走路，可能是腳痛。
examples.english_sentence: He always walks with a limp; maybe his foot hurts.

mandarin_meaning: 走開；滾開；被趕走
english_meaning: to scram / to get out / to be kicked out
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，通常用來叫人離開或形容某人被趕走，語氣可粗魯或不耐煩。有時也用來描述自己離開。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to tell someone to leave (scram) or to describe being kicked out. Often coarse or impatient in tone; can also mean to leave oneself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好煩，趷路啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faan4, hot3 lou6 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別煩我，走開啦！
examples.english_sentence: Don't bother me, scram!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺酒吧鬧交，被保安趷路咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zau2 baa1 naau6 gaau1, bei6 bou2 on1 hot3 lou6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在酒吧吵架，被保安趕出去了。
examples.english_sentence: He argued in the bar and was kicked out by security.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆話佢做錯事，叫佢趷路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 waa6 keoi5 zou6 co3 si6, giu3 keoi5 hot3 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板說他做錯了，叫他滾開／離開。
examples.english_sentence: The boss said he messed up and told him to get out.

mandarin_meaning: 生悶氣；耍小性子；噘嘴或擺臭臉
english_meaning: to sulk; to pout; to act petty or give someone the cold shoulder
explanation_mandarin: 「趷頭」是廣東話口語，指因不高興或不滿而噘嘴、擺臭臉或故意不說話，常用來形容小孩或情侶間耍小性子的狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to sulk or pout—behaving sullenly, giving someone the cold shoulder, or acting petulant. Often used for children or between partners/friends when someone is upset and withdraws.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔開心就趷頭，唔肯同我講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 hoi1 sam1 zau6 kot3 tau4, m4 hang2 tung4 ngo5 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不高興就生悶氣，不肯跟我說話。
examples.english_sentence: He sulks when he's unhappy and refuses to talk to me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路仔唔如願就會趷頭，要哄先肯笑返。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 zai2 m4 jyu4 jyun6 zau6 wui5 kot3 tau4, jiu3 hung2 sin1 hang2 siu3 faan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子不如願就會耍小性子，要哄才會笑回來。
examples.english_sentence: Children will pout if things don't go their way; you have to coax them before they smile again.

mandarin_meaning: 擺架子；擺高姿態；故意疏遠或看不起別人
english_meaning: to put on airs; to act high-and-mighty; to snub or be aloof
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人擺架子、故意擺高姿態或疏遠、看不起別人，語氣常帶輕蔑或不屑。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang verb describing someone who puts on airs, acts arrogant or aloof, or snubs others — often with a tone of disdain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日趷高，唔同我哋講話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 hot3 gou1, m4 tung4 ngo5 dei6 gong2 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近常常擺架子，不跟我們說話。
examples.english_sentence: He's been acting all high-and-mighty lately and not talking to us.

mandarin_meaning: 盤腿坐（多用於佛教或打坐）
english_meaning: to sit cross-legged (as in meditation/lotus posture)
explanation_mandarin: 趺常見於詞語如「趺坐」、「跏趺坐」，指盤腿而坐，多用於佛教、打坐或靜坐的語境。
explanation_english: The character refers to sitting cross-legged (as in meditation). Appears in compounds like 趺坐 or 跏趺坐, used in Buddhist/meditative contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日趺坐打坐，保持心境平靜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 fu1 co5 daa2 co5, bou2 ci4 sam1 ging2 ping4 zing6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常盤腿打坐，保持心境平靜。
examples.english_sentence: He often sits cross-legged to meditate, keeping his mind calm.

mandarin_meaning: 趁（利用、趁著）
english_meaning: to take advantage of; to seize (an opportunity)
explanation_mandarin: 表示利用某個時機或情況去做某事，跟「趁」相同或相近的用法，屬於書面或古漢語中可見的字形變體。
explanation_english: Used to indicate taking advantage of an opportunity or situation to do something. It is a variant form related to 趁 and appears in some written/archaic usages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 趻依家有時間，快啲把功課做完。
examples.jyutping_sentence: can3 ji1 gaa1 jau5 si4 gaan3, faai3 di1 baa2 gung1 fo3 zou6 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 趁現在有時間，快點把功課做完。
examples.english_sentence: Take advantage of having time now and finish your homework quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 跺脚；用脚跺地（表示不耐烦、愤怒或烦躁）
english_meaning: to stamp/stomp one's foot (expressing impatience, anger, or restlessness)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，指用力用腳跺地，常表達不耐煩、氣惱或小孩發脾氣時的動作。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to stomp or stamp one's foot, often used to show impatience, annoyance, or a child's tantrum.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個細路唔畀糖食，就喺度趻腳喊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 sai3 lou5 m4 bei2 tong4 sik6, zau6 hai2 dou6 ceon2 goek3 haam3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子不讓他吃糖，就在那裡跺腳哭。
examples.english_sentence: The child wasn't allowed to have candy, so he stood there stamping his feet and crying.

mandarin_meaning: 趾（脚趾）
english_meaning: toe (digit of the foot)
explanation_mandarin: 表示脚的最末端的趾，常與「脚」結合為「脚趾」，指腳上的趾頭部位。
explanation_english: Refers to a toe, a digit at the end of the foot; commonly used together with "foot" as "toe".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心踢到隻腳趾，好痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 tek3 dou3 zek3 goek3 zi2, hou2 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不小心踢到一只脚趾，很痛。
examples.english_sentence: I accidentally kicked my toe; it hurts a lot.

mandarin_meaning: 腳趾的指甲（趾甲、腳趾甲）
english_meaning: toenail
explanation_mandarin: 指覆蓋在腳趾端的硬質角質層，即腳趾的指甲，常需修剪或護理。
explanation_english: The hard keratinous plate on a toe — a toenail. It covers the tip of a toe and often requires trimming or care.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啲趾甲太長，今晚要剪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 di1 zi2 gaap3 taai3 coeng4, gam1 maan5 jiu3 zin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的趾甲太長，今晚要剪。
examples.english_sentence: My toenails are too long; I need to trim them tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢隻趾甲倒生，要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zek3 zi2 gaap3 dou2 saang1, jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的趾甲長成內生趾甲，要去看醫生。
examples.english_sentence: His toenail became ingrown; he needs to see a doctor.

mandarin_meaning: 得意洋洋；驕傲自滿
english_meaning: to be smug or arrogant; to strut around proudly
explanation_mandarin: 形容人得意、自滿或傲慢地表現，顯得高高在上、擺架子。常用來批評某人驕傲或愛炫耀。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is smug, conceited, or arrogantly triumphant — literally 'walking on tiptoe with pride.' Often used to criticize a person for being pompous or showy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 贏咗比賽之後，佢成日趾高氣揚，令人好反感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jing4 zo2 bei2 coi3 zi1 hau6, keoi5 sing4 jat6 zi2 gou1 hei3 joeng4, ling6 jan4 hou2 faan2 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比赛赢了之后，他整天趾高气扬，让人很反感。
examples.english_sentence: After winning the competition, he strutted around all the time, which was very off-putting.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/方言）穿（拖鞋）；拖着脚走
english_meaning: to wear/slip on (slippers); to drag one's feet (when walking)
explanation_mandarin: ‘趿’多用于粤语口语，常见用法如‘趿鞋’表示穿拖鞋，或表示拖着脚走的动作（如‘趿脚行路’）。
explanation_english: Commonly used in Cantonese speech. Often appears in phrases like '趿鞋' (to wear/slip on slippers) or to describe dragging one's feet when walking (e.g., '趿腳行路').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日趿腳行路，睇落好懶散。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 taa1 goek3 haang4 lou6, tai2 lok6 hou2 laan5 saan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常拖着脚走路，看起来很懒散。
examples.english_sentence: He often drags his feet when walking; he looks very lazy.

synonyms: 拖腳/拖着脚 (to drag one's feet)

mandarin_meaning: 跆（tái）——本義與踢、踩有關，現多見於複合詞如「跆拳道」(Taekwondo)。
english_meaning: 跆 (toi4) — originally related to kicking/stomping; commonly appears in the compound 'Taekwondo'.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 詞素 / 專有名詞（在「跆拳道」等詞中作名詞成分）
partOfSpeech_english: noun (as part of the proper name 'Taekwondo'); rarely used as a verb/root
explanation_mandarin: 「跆」字古義與踢、踩相關，單獨少用，現代漢語中主要見於「跆拳道」一詞，表示與踢腿、腿法相關的含義。
explanation_english: The character 跆 historically relates to kicking or stamping. It is rarely used alone in modern Chinese and is most commonly seen in the compound '跆拳道' (Taekwondo), referring to kicking/leg techniques.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想去學跆拳道。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 hok6 toi4 kyun4 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想去学跆拳道。
examples.english_sentence: I want to learn Taekwondo.

mandarin_meaning: 跆拳道 (táiquándào)
english_meaning: Taekwondo (Korean martial art and sport)
explanation_mandarin: 源自韓國的武術與競技運動，強調以腿法為主，結合拳打、防守與比賽規則，可用於自衛、健身與比賽。
explanation_english: A Korean martial art and sport that emphasizes kicking techniques along with punches and defensive moves; practiced for self-defense, fitness, and competition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細個學過跆拳道，對體能同自衛好有幫助。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 hok6 gwo3 toi4 kyun4 dou6, deoi3 tai2 nang4 tung4 zi6 wai6 hou2 jau5 bong1 zo6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小時候學過跆拳道，對體能和自衛很有幫助。
examples.english_sentence: I learned taekwondo when I was young; it really helped my fitness and self-defense.

mandarin_meaning: 跋（書後的短文，稱為跋文）；古義有跋扈、踐踏之意
english_meaning: afterword/postscript (in a book); (archaic/compound) to trample or overbearing (as in '跋扈')
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词 / 动词（視用法而定）
explanation_mandarin: “跋”常指書籍末尾由作者或他人撰寫的短文（跋文）。在古漢語或合成詞中，如“跋扈”，含有霸道、蠻橫的意思；此外亦有與踐踏相關的古義。
explanation_english: “跋” commonly refers to an afterword or short concluding piece in a book (跋文). In older usage or in compounds like “跋扈”, it conveys being overbearing or trampling; it also has an archaic sense related to treading.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺書尾寫咗一篇跋，講述寫作動機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 syu1 mei5 se2 zo2 jat1 pin1 baat3, gong2 seot6 se2 zok3 dung6 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在书尾写了一篇跋，讲述写作动机。
examples.english_sentence: He wrote an afterword at the end of the book, explaining his reasons for writing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個老細好跋扈，啲員工唔敢反對。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 lou5 sai3 hou2 baat3 wu6, di1 jyun4 gung1 m4 gam2 faan2 deoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个老板很跋扈，员工不敢反对。
examples.english_sentence: That boss is very overbearing; employees don't dare oppose him.

mandarin_meaning: 掉落、摔倒、下降
english_meaning: to fall; to drop; to decline
explanation_mandarin: 表示從高處向下掉落或人失去平衡而摔倒，也可用來表示數量、價格等的下降。
explanation_english: Indicates falling or dropping from a higher position or a person losing balance and falling; can also denote a decrease (e.g., in quantity or price).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢行路唔小心跌咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hang4 lou6 m4 siu2 sam1 dit3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走路不小心摔倒了。
examples.english_sentence: He fell because he wasn't careful while walking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 股票跌咗好多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 piu3 dit3 zo2 hou2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 股票跌了很多。
examples.english_sentence: The stocks fell a lot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個手機由枱度跌落地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 sau2 gei1 jau4 toi2 dou6 dit3 lok6 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 手机从桌上掉到地上。
examples.english_sentence: The phone fell off the table onto the floor.

mandarin_meaning: 丢脸；出丑；尴尬
english_meaning: to embarrass oneself; to lose face; to flop (a joke or performance)
explanation_mandarin: 「跌watt」是香港粵語俗語，用於形容某人表現失敗、說話或表演尷尬而讓自己丟臉。常用於口語和網路語境。
explanation_english: “跌watt” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang describing someone who embarrasses themselves or whose joke/performance flops, causing loss of face. Common in spoken and online contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲笑話完全跌watt，大家都冇反應。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 siu3waa6 jyun4cyun4 dit3 wat6, daai6gaa1 dou1 mou5 faan2jing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的笑話完全出洋相，大家都沒有反應。
examples.english_sentence: His jokes totally flopped; nobody reacted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講緊嘢講到冷場，真係跌watt。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 gan2 je5 gong2 dou3 laang5 coeng4, zan1 hai6 dit3 wat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 講話講到冷場，真的很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: The talk went awkward and fell flat — it was really embarrassing.

mandarin_meaning: 摔倒；掉下；（也可引申）下跌、下降
english_meaning: to fall down; to drop; (figuratively) to decline or slump
explanation_mandarin: 表示人或物從高處掉下、摔倒，也可用於比喻，表示價格、數值或狀況下降或變差。
explanation_english: Describes a person or object falling down from a height or taking a tumble; can also be used figuratively to describe prices, values, or conditions dropping or worsening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隻貓喺樓梯度跌低咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zek3 maau1 hai2 lau4 tai1 dou6 dit3 dai1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那只猫在楼梯上摔倒了。
examples.english_sentence: The cat fell down on the stairs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近啲股票跌低咗，大家都好擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 di1 gu2 piu3 dit3 dai1 zo2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hou2 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近股票下跌了，大家都很担心。
examples.english_sentence: Stock prices have dropped recently; everyone is worried.

mandarin_meaning: 摔倒
english_meaning: to fall down; to trip and fall
explanation_mandarin: 指失去平衡或被絆倒而落到地上，可能造成受傷。
explanation_english: To lose balance or be tripped and fall to the ground; may result in injury.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢行路唔小心跌倒咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hang4 lou6 m4 siu2 sam1 dit3 dou2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走路不小心摔倒了。
examples.english_sentence: He fell down because he wasn't careful while walking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街口好滑，成日有人跌倒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 hau2 hou2 waat6, sing4 jat6 jau5 jan4 dit3 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 路口很滑，经常有人摔倒。
examples.english_sentence: The corner is very slippery; people often fall there.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我踩到香蕉皮跌倒，腳扭傷咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 caai2 dou3 hoeng1 ziu1 pei4 dit3 dou2, goek3 nau2 soeng1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我踩到香蕉皮摔倒，腳扭傷了。
examples.english_sentence: I stepped on a banana peel and fell, twisting my ankle.

mandarin_meaning: （商品或資產）價格下跌；（口語）自我或形象變得廉價、貶值
english_meaning: (1) (of goods/assets) to drop in price; (2) (colloquial) to make oneself or one's image seem cheap/lose value
explanation_mandarin: 「跌價」可指價格下降，例如商品或股票價格下跌；在口語中也可用來形容為了某人或某事而讓自己顯得廉價、貶低自己。
explanation_english: "跌價" can mean a drop in price (for goods, stocks, etc.). Colloquially it can also mean to cheapen oneself or lower one's dignity/value for someone or something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部手機跌價咗，依家平咗一千蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 sau2 gei1 dip3 gaa3 zo2, ji4 gaa1 peng4 zo2 jat1 cin1 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那部手机跌价了，现在便宜了一千块。
examples.english_sentence: That phone has dropped in price; it's a thousand dollars cheaper now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想為咗佢跌價。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 wai6 zo2 keoi5 dip3 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想为了他/她而贬低自己。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to cheapen myself for him/her.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隻股票跌價，投資者好擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zek3 gu2 piu3 dip3 gaa3, tau4 zi1 ze2 hou2 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那只股票跌价了，投资者很担心。
examples.english_sentence: That stock's price fell; investors are worried.

mandarin_meaning: 下跌趨勢；走勢下滑
english_meaning: downward trend; decline; falling momentum
explanation_mandarin: 「跌勢」通常指價格、股市、銷量或局勢等呈現下降的趨勢或下滑的勢頭。
explanation_english: “跌勢” refers to a downward trend or declining momentum, often used for prices, markets, sales, or general situations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家股市跌勢好勁，投資要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 gu2 si5 dit3 sai3 hou2 ging6, tau4 zi1 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在股市下跌趨勢很猛，投資要小心。
examples.english_sentence: The stock market is in a sharp downward trend right now; investors should be careful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間公司嘅銷量出現跌勢，可能要裁員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 gung1 si1 ge3 siu1 loeng6 ceot1 jin2 dit3 sai3, ho2 nang4 jiu3 coi4 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間公司的銷量出現下跌趨勢，可能要裁員。
examples.english_sentence: This company's sales have shown a downward trend; they might need to lay off staff.

mandarin_meaning: 掉了；摔倒了；下跌了（视语境而定）
english_meaning: fell; has fallen; dropped (depends on context)
explanation_mandarin: 「跌咗」是粤语的完成體，表示某物或某人已经跌下来或摔倒，或指价格等下跌，视上下文而定。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '跌咗' is the perfective form of '跌' (to fall). It indicates that something or someone has fallen/dropped or that a price has fallen, depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個杯跌咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 bui1 dit3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 杯子掉了。
examples.english_sentence: The cup fell.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街度跌咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 dou6 dit3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街上摔倒了。
examples.english_sentence: He fell on the street.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝股價跌咗好多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 gu2 gaa3 dit3 zo2 hou2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上股价下跌了很多。
examples.english_sentence: The stock price fell a lot this morning.

jyutping: dit3 zo2 go3 caang4 zap1 faan1 go3 gat1
mandarin_meaning: 丢了橙子，捡到桔子；比喻失去更好的東西，得到次一等的代替品（將就、權宜之計）
english_meaning: ‘Lost an orange, picked up a tangerine’ — used to say someone lost something better and had to settle for an inferior substitute
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容本來有更好或理想的選擇，但最後沒得到，只好接受較次的替代品或妥協。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning you missed out on a better option and ended up with a lesser substitute — to make do or settle for less.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我原本想買部高階相機，但賣晒，最後跌咗個橙執番個桔，只好買咗部入門機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jyun4 bun2 soeng2 maai5 bou6 gou1 gaai1 soeng2 gei1, daan6 maai5 saai3, zeoi3 hau6 dit3 zo2 go3 caang4 zap1 faan1 go3 gat1, zi2 hou2 maai5 zo2 bou6 jap6 mun4 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我原本想買那台高階相機，但都賣光了，最後丟了橙子、撿回桔子，只好買了入門款的相機。
examples.english_sentence: I originally wanted that high-end camera, but it sold out. In the end I lost the orange and picked up the tangerine — I had to buy an entry-level camera.

jyutping: dip3 zo2 go3 caang4 zap1 faan1 go3 gat1
mandarin_meaning: 失去一個較好的東西，撿回較差的替代品（得不償失）
english_meaning: To lose something better and end up with an inferior substitute; a poor trade-off or consolation prize
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容失去較好或重要的東西，卻得到較差或次要的代替品；常用來批評某種得不償失或將就的結果。
explanation_english: Used to describe losing something better and receiving an inferior replacement; commonly used to criticize a poor trade-off or a make-do outcome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我本來諗住轉工搵好啲，但最後跌咗個橙執返個桔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bun2 loi4 lam2 zyu6 zyun2 gung1 wan2 hou2 di1, daan6 zeoi3 hau6 dip3 zo2 go3 caang4 zap1 faan1 go3 gat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我本來想換工作找更好的，但最後卻是失去一個橙，撿回一個桔。
examples.english_sentence: I originally planned to switch jobs for a better one, but in the end I lost something good and only got a worse substitute.

mandarin_meaning: （事件、情節）起伏曲折；（文風、情感）豪放不拘
english_meaning: full of ups and downs; winding and dramatic (of events or plots); also majestic and unrestrained (literary)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容事情、情節或情感有起伏、波折，或形容文風豪放、不拘一格。
explanation_english: Used to describe events, plots, or emotions that have ups and downs or twists; can also describe a majestic, unrestrained literary/style or tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本小說情節跌宕起伏，好吸引。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 siu2 syut3 cing4 zit3 dit3 dong6 hei2 fuk1, hou2 kap1 jan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這本小說情節跌宕起伏，非常吸引人。
examples.english_sentence: This novel's plot is full of twists and turns and very compelling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅人生跌宕起伏，但佢從未放棄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 jan4 saang1 dit3 dong6 hei2 fuk1, daan6 keoi5 cung4 mei6 fong3 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的人生跌宕起伏，但他從未放棄。
examples.english_sentence: His life has had many ups and downs, but he never gave up.

mandarin_meaning: 股市下跌 / 市場下滑
english_meaning: market downturn; falling stock market (bear market conditions)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，指股市或整體市場價格下跌的情況，常用於形容一段時間內市場表現疲弱。
explanation_english: Colloquial term referring to a falling stock market or general market downturn; used to describe a period of weak market performance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家跌市，大家都唔敢亂買股票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 dit3 si5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 gam2 lyun6 maai5 gu2 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在股市下跌，大家都不敢隨便買股票。
examples.english_sentence: With the market falling now, everyone is hesitant to buy stocks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果跌市繼續，可能會有更多公司裁員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 dit3 si5 gai3 zuk6, ho2 nang4 wui5 jau5 gang3 do1 gung1 si1 coi4 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果股市持續下跌，可能會有更多公司裁員。
examples.english_sentence: If the market continues to fall, there may be more company layoffs.

mandarin_meaning: 跌幅（下降的幅度，例如價格或指數的下跌幅度）
english_meaning: amount or percentage of a decline (e.g., in price, stock index, or value)
explanation_mandarin: 表示某項數值（如股價、指數、價格等）下降的幅度，常用來描述跌落的百分比或點數。
explanation_english: Refers to the magnitude of a decrease in a value (such as a stock price, index, or price); commonly used to describe the percentage or points dropped.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝恆指嘅跌幅好大，跌咗超過一千點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 hang4 zi2 ge3 dit3 fuk1 hou2 daai6, dit3 zo2 ciu1 gwo3 jat1 cin1 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天恒指的跌幅很大，跌了超过一千点。
examples.english_sentence: The Hang Seng Index fell sharply this morning, with a drop of over a thousand points.

mandarin_meaning: 中醫外治法，專指針對跌打損傷的整骨、推拿、按摩等治療（也泛指從事這類治療的師傅或門診）
english_meaning: Traditional Chinese bone-setting and trauma treatment (includes massage, manipulation, bone-setting); also refers to practitioners who perform such treatments (Dit Da)
explanation_mandarin: 「跌打」源自粵語，原指治療跌打損傷的外治方法，包括整骨、推拿、按摩、點藥等，民間常有「跌打師傅」為病患調理筋骨和外傷。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term referring to folk/TCM external treatments for trauma and sprains—bone-setting, massage, manipulation, topical remedies. It can also denote the practitioner (Dit Da master) who treats such injuries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢上個月踢波扭親腳，去睇跌打師傅，宜家好返晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng6 go3 jyut6 tek3 bo1 nau2 can1 goek3, heoi3 tai2 dit3 daa2 si1 fu1, ji4 gaa1 hou2 faan1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上个月踢球把脚扭伤了，去看了跌打师傅，現在好多了。
examples.english_sentence: He twisted his ankle playing football last month, went to see a Dit Da practitioner, and is much better now.

mandarin_meaning: 跌打酒 / 跌打藥酒（中藥或民間藥酒，用於活血化瘀、消腫止痛，外敷於跌打損傷、扭傷、瘀青等）
english_meaning: Dit da wine (medicinal liniment wine used in Chinese folk/traditional medicine to promote circulation, reduce swelling and relieve pain; applied externally to bruises, sprains, and other traumatic injuries)
explanation_mandarin: 跌打酒是中醫及民間常用的一種藥用酒，內含多種中藥材，用於活血化瘀、消腫止痛，通常外敷或按摩時使用，常見於跌打損傷和扭傷的處理。
explanation_english: A type of medicinal wine used in traditional Chinese and folk medicine, typically containing herbal ingredients to invigorate blood, dispel bruising, reduce swelling and ease pain. It is usually applied externally or used during massage and bonesetting for injuries such as bruises and sprains.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你撞親要唔要我拎跌打酒畀你搽？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zong6 can1 jiu3 m4 jiu3 ngo5 ling1 dit3 daa2 zau2 bei2 nei5 caat3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你撞到了要不要我拿跌打酒給你擦？
examples.english_sentence: Did you get bumped? Do you want me to bring you some dit da wine to rub on it?

mandarin_meaning: （口語）摔得很慘；慘敗、失敗得很慘
english_meaning: to fall badly; to take a nasty tumble; (figurative) to be crushed/defeated badly
explanation_mandarin: 「跌渣」是香港粵語口語，通常指身體上摔得很慘或比喻在某事上慘敗、失敗得很難看。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to fall badly (physically) or, figuratively, to suffer a crushing defeat or fail spectacularly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個細路喺街跌渣，膝頭都擦破晒，喊唔停。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 sai3 lou6 hai2 gaai1 dit3 zaa1, sat1 tau4 dou1 caat3 po3 saai3, haam3 m4 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友在街上摔得很慘，膝蓋都擦破了，一直哭個不停。
examples.english_sentence: The kid took a nasty tumble on the street — his knees were scraped and he wouldn't stop crying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺比賽輸到跌渣，面都冇得見人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 bei2 coi3 syu1 dou3 dit3 zaa1, min6 dou1 mou5 dak1 gin3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在比賽中輸得很慘，沒臉見人。
examples.english_sentence: He lost so badly in the match that he was completely humiliated.

mandarin_meaning: 令人吃驚；大吃一驚；出乎意料
english_meaning: to be surprised; to be astonished; to be taken aback (lit. 'to drop one's glasses')
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，字面是「眼鏡跌了」，引申為對某事感到非常驚訝或出乎意料。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning 'glasses fall'; used to say one is very surprised or taken aback by something unexpected.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次考試考到咁高分，真係跌眼鏡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 haau2 dou3 gam2 gou1 fan1, zan1 hai6 dit3 ngaan5 geng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這次考試考得這麼高分，真讓人吃驚。
examples.english_sentence: He got such a high score on the exam this time — really surprising.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到佢話辭職嘅消息，我真係跌眼鏡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 keoi5 waa6 ci4 zik1 ge3 siu1 sik1, ngo5 zan1 hai6 dit3 ngaan5 geng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到他要辭職的消息，我真的非常驚訝。
examples.english_sentence: When I heard he was resigning, I was really taken aback.

mandarin_meaning: 被解雇／被炒魷魚
english_meaning: to be fired; to be sacked
explanation_mandarin: 「跌紙」是香港口語俗語，用來表示被公司或機構解僱、失去工作。相當於粵語常用的「炒魷魚」。
explanation_english: “跌紙” is Hong Kong colloquial slang meaning to be dismissed from a job or sacked. It is roughly equivalent to the Cantonese expression “炒魷魚.”

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱喺公司跌紙咗，依家搵緊新工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 hai2 gung1 si1 dit3 zi2 zo2, ji1 gaa1 wan2 gan2 san1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛在公司被解雇了，現在正在找新工作。
examples.english_sentence: He was just fired from the company and is now looking for a new job.

jyutping: dit3 lok6 dei6 laa1 faan1 zaak3 saa1
mandarin_meaning: 跌得又狼狽又滿身泥灰（比喻遭遇慘敗或極為丟臉）
english_meaning: to fall flat and get covered in dirt (figuratively: to suffer a humiliating defeat or be thoroughly embarrassed)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面是跌落地再被弄得滿身沙塵，通常用來形容跌倒狼狽或比喻遭遇慘敗、極為丟臉。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally describing falling to the ground and getting sand/dirt all over. Often used to describe a very embarrassing fall or, figuratively, a humiliating defeat or utter humiliation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街口跌落地揦翻拃沙，尷尬到唔知點算。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 hau2 dit3 lok6 dei6 laa1 faan1 zaak3 saa1, gaan1 gaai3 dou3 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街口摔倒，摔得灰頭土臉，尷尬得不知道怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: He fell at the street corner and ended up covered in dirt; he was so embarrassed he didn't know what to do.

jyutping: dit3 lok6 dei6 laa1 faan1 zaap3 saa1
mandarin_meaning: 摔倒後爬起來繼續（做某事）；比喻遭受挫折但迅速恢復或重整旗鼓
english_meaning: to fall to the ground and pick up sand — figuratively, to be knocked down but quickly get back up and carry on; to bounce back from a setback
explanation_mandarin: 此片語字面描述跌落在地並抓起地上的沙，常用作比喻，指人在遭遇失敗或受挫後迅速恢復、重新開始或堅持下去。多見於廣東話口語或地方俗語中，帶有不屈不撓的語氣。
explanation_english: Literally describes falling to the ground and grabbing sand; used figuratively to mean being knocked down but quickly getting back up and continuing. Common in colloquial Cantonese as a slang/idiomatic expression conveying resilience or determination after a setback.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽遲咗報名，唔代表放棄——跌落地揦返拃沙，再試一次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 ci4 zo2 bou3 ming4, m4 doi6 biu2 fong3 hei3 —— dit3 lok6 dei6 laa1 faan1 zaap3 saa1, zoi3 si3 jat1 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽晚報名不代表放棄——摔倒了就爬起來再試一次。
examples.english_sentence: Registering late for the contest doesn't mean giving up — if you get knocked down, get back up and try again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司呢次業績差，但老細話唔好氣餒，要跌落地揦返拃沙，重整策略。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ni1 ci3 jip6 zik1 caa1, daan6 lou5 sai3 waa6 m4 hou2 hei3 noi6, jiu3 dit3 lok6 dei6 laa1 faan1 zaap3 saa1, cung4 zeng2 caak3 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司這次業績不好，但老闆說不要氣餒，要跌倒了就爬起來，重整策略。
examples.english_sentence: The company's results were poor this time, but the boss said don't be discouraged — pick yourselves up and reorganize the strategy.

mandarin_meaning: 形容走路或行動不穩、東倒西歪或做事笨拙、不順利（可作副詞或形容詞）。
english_meaning: staggering or stumbling; unsteady; doing something in a haphazard, clumsy, or awkward way (can be used as an adverb or adjective).
explanation_mandarin: 常用來形容人走路不穩、搖搖晃晃或者辦事磕磕碰碰、不順暢的情況。
explanation_english: Used to describe walking or moving unsteadily (stumbling, staggering) or doing things clumsily and without smoothness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢醉咗，跌跌撞撞行返屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 zo2, dit3 dit3 zong6 zong6 haang4 faan1 uk1 kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他喝醉了，跌跌撞撞地走回家。
examples.english_sentence: He was drunk and staggered home, stumbling.

mandarin_meaning: 摔倒；跌倒（也可引申为遭遇挫折或犯错误）
english_meaning: to fall down; to trip (can also be used figuratively for a setback or mistake)
explanation_mandarin: 表示身體失去平衡而摔倒，也常用於比喻遭遇挫折、犯錯或遭受損失。
explanation_english: Refers to losing one's balance and falling down; also commonly used figuratively to mean suffering a setback, making a mistake, or taking a loss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢行路唔小心跌跤，手腳都擦破咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haang4 lou6 m4 siu2 sam1 dit3 gaau1, sau2 goek3 dou1 caat3 po3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走路不小心跌倒，手腳都擦破了。
examples.english_sentence: He/She wasn't careful walking and fell, scraping his/her hands and feet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心啲，唔好跌跤！
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 di1, m4 hou2 dit3 gaau1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心點，別跌倒！
examples.english_sentence: Be careful, don't fall!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司喺呢個項目度跌咗一跤，損失幾十萬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 hai2 ni1 go3 hoeng6 muk6 dou6 dit3 zo2 jat1 gaau1, syun2 sat1 gei2 sap6 maan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司在这个项目上吃了一次亏，损失好几十万。
examples.english_sentence: The company suffered a setback on this project, losing hundreds of thousands.

mandarin_meaning: （動）蹉跎、浪費（光陰）；常見於「蹉跎」等詞
english_meaning: to waste time; to let time slip away (often used in compounds like '蹉跎')
explanation_mandarin: 表示荒廢光陰、虛度時光，通常與「蹉」連用成「蹉跎」。
explanation_english: Indicates wasting or squandering time; commonly appears in the compound '蹉跎' meaning to let the years or time slip away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再蹉跎光陰，趁而家開始做啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi6 co1 to4 gwong1 jam1, can3 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 ci2 zo6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要再蹉跎光陰，趁現在開始做吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't waste any more time; start doing it now.

mandarin_meaning: 懒散、游手好闲的人；游手好闲、不务正业的人
english_meaning: a loafer; an idler; someone who loafs around and shirks work
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，通常用來形容成天懶散、不肯做事或遊手好閒的人，有時帶輕蔑或戲謔語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe someone who is lazy, idle, or shirks responsibilities. Often carries a mildly contemptuous or teasing tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺屋企懶懶地，真係一個跎仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei5 laan5 laan5 dei6, zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 to4 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天待在家裡懶懶散散，真是個游手好閒的人。
examples.english_sentence: He stays at home all day being lazy — he's really a loafer.

mandarin_meaning: 偷懶、混日子、拖延、不積極
english_meaning: to slack off; to dawdle; to loaf around and avoid work or responsibilities
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話俗語，指人懶散、偷懶、不積極做事或拖延時間，類似「偷懶／擺爛」的意思。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term meaning to be lazy or slack off — to dawdle, procrastinate, or loaf around instead of doing work or fulfilling responsibilities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢排佢成日跎槍，老細都唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 paai4 keoi5 sing4 jat6 to1 coeng1, lou5 sai3 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近他總是偷懶，老闆都不高興。
examples.english_sentence: Lately he has been slacking off all the time; the boss is not happy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再跎槍啦，快啲交份報告。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 to1 coeng1 laa1, faai3 di1 gaau1 fan6 bou3 gou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再偷懶了，快點交份報告。
examples.english_sentence: Stop slacking off and hand in the report quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 游手好闲的人；懒散的人
english_meaning: loafer; idler; slacker — a person who habitually wastes time or avoids work
explanation_mandarin: “跎炮”為廣東話俚語，通常用來形容成天閒蕩、不做正經事或懶散遊手好閒的人，帶貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who loafs around, shirks responsibilities, or habitually wastes time. It is colloquial and usually derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺屋企跎炮，唔做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei5 to1 paau3, m4 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天在家游手好闲，不做事。
examples.english_sentence: He loafs around at home all day and doesn't do any work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做跎炮啦，快啲搵工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 to1 paau3 laa1, faai3 di1 wan2 gung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別當懶鬼了，快點找工作吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a slacker — go and find a job quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 拖拉鬼 / 慢性子
english_meaning: slowpoke; dawdler; someone who is sluggish or procrastinates
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，形容做事拖拉、行動緩慢或效率低的人。常用作口語稱呼或評語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe a person who is slow, dawdles, or procrastinates — someone who moves or works sluggishly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日跎鐵，做嘢老係趕唔切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 to4 tit3, zou6 je5 lou5 hai6 gon2 m4 cit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天拖拖拉拉，做事總是趕不及。
examples.english_sentence: He's always dawdling; he never finishes tasks on time.

mandarin_meaning: 跑 (pǎo)
english_meaning: run; run away; flee
explanation_mandarin: 表示用腳快速移動或奔跑；也可用於表示逃離、跑掉或趕快離開的意思，視語境而定。
explanation_english: Indicates running or moving quickly on foot; can also mean to flee or to leave quickly depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋快啲跑入去避雨啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 faai3 di1 paau2 jap6 heoi3 bei6 jyu5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們快點跑進去避雨吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's run inside quickly to take shelter from the rain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個仔好鍾意跑步。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 zai2 hou2 zung1 ji3 paau2 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的兒子很喜歡跑步。
examples.english_sentence: His son really likes running.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果有危險，最好即刻跑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 jau5 ngai4 him2, zeoi3 hou2 zik1 hak1 paau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果有危險，最好立刻跑。
examples.english_sentence: If there's danger, it's best to run immediately.

mandarin_meaning: 過季；不再流行或銷售淡薄（口語）
english_meaning: out of season; no longer in demand or fashionable; past the peak season
explanation_mandarin: 「跑季」是香港粵語口語說法，通常用來形容商品、款式或趨勢已經過了當季，銷量下降或不再流行，也可指錯過季節性機會。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese slang, "跑季" describes items, styles, or trends that are out of season — demand has dropped or they are no longer fashionable. It can also mean having missed a seasonal opportunity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢批衫已經跑季，賣唔到幾多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 pat1 saam1 ji5 ging1 paau2 gwai3, maai6 m4 dou2 gei2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這批衣服已經過季，賣不掉多少。
examples.english_sentence: This batch of clothes is already out of season; they aren't selling much.

mandarin_meaning: 在山路上（通常指以摩托車或汽車）高速行駛或飆車
english_meaning: to drive/race at high speed on mountain roads (often illegal); to go trail running (literal)
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，通常指在山路上以高速駕駛或飆車，常帶有非法或危險的含義；字面上也可指到山上跑步或越野跑。
explanation_english: A slang term typically meaning to drive or race at high speed on mountain roads (often illegal and dangerous); literally can also mean to go running or trail-running in the mountains.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成日夜晚去大帽山跑山，好危險！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 seng4 jat6 je6 maan5 heoi3 daai6 mou6 saan1 paau2 saan1, hou2 ngai4 him2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们经常在大帽山的山路上晚上飙车，很危险！
examples.english_sentence: They often go to Tai Mo Shan at night to race on the mountain roads; it's very dangerous!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我星期日想去郊外跑山，順便郁下筋骨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing1 kei4 jat6 soeng2 heoi3 gaau1 ngoi6 paau2 saan1, seon6 bin6 juk6 haa6 gan1 gwat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我星期天想去郊外跑山，顺便活动一下筋骨。
examples.english_sentence: I want to go trail running in the countryside on Sunday to get some exercise.

mandarin_meaning: 指專門在山路上非法飆車的車輛或參與此行為的人／群體（俚語）；也可指為此用途而改裝或沒有正式牌照的車輛。
english_meaning: Slang for vehicles or people who take part in illegal mountain-road racing; can also refer to modified or unlicensed vehicles used for such racing.
explanation_mandarin: 「跑山牌」在香港粵語中常用來形容那些專門在郊區山路（如大欖、帽山等）夜間飆車的摩托車或私家車，或指涉參與者。語氣帶有貶義及街頭俚語色彩，亦涉及非法改裝或無牌情況。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "跑山牌" is used to describe motorcycles or cars that regularly race on rural/ mountain roads at night, or the people who take part. The term is slang with negative connotations and often implies illegal modification or unlicensed vehicles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢架機車係跑山牌，成日夜晚跑山。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gaa3 gei1 ce1 hai6 paau2 saan1 paai4 , sing4 jat6 je6 maan5 paau2 saan1 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的摩托車是「跑山牌」，總是在晚上跑山（飆車）。
examples.english_sentence: His motorcycle is a "paau saan paai" — he's always going mountain racing at night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方加強巡邏，打擊跑山牌同非法飆車活動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 gaa1 koeng4 seon4 lo4 , daa2 gik1 paau2 saan1 paai4 tung4 fei1 faat3 biu1 ce1 wut6 dung6 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方加強巡邏，打擊跑山牌和非法飆車活動。
examples.english_sentence: The police increased patrols to crack down on "paau saan paai" and illegal racing activities.

mandarin_meaning: 跑腿；催款/收款；跑單、跑客（完成業績）
english_meaning: to run errands; to collect payment/press for payment; to canvass clients or handle accounts (complete sales/quota)
explanation_mandarin: 「跑數」是廣東話口語，根據語境有幾個常見意思：1) 跑腿、外出辦事或代人處理瑣碎事務；2) 去催收款項或收取欠款；3) 在生意/銷售上跑客、跑單以完成業績。用法多見於口語和工作場景。
explanation_english: “跑數” is Cantonese colloquial/slang. Depending on context it commonly means: 1) to run errands or do tasks on someone’s behalf; 2) to collect or chase payments; 3) in business/sales, to canvass clients or handle accounts to meet targets. It is mainly used in spoken and workplace contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日要幫老細跑數，去銀行交啲文件。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 bong1 lou5 sai3 paau2 sou3, heoi3 ngan4 hong4 gaau1 di1 man4 gin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天要幫老闆跑腿，去銀行交一些文件。
examples.english_sentence: I have to run errands for the boss today — go to the bank to submit some documents.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個客戶遲咗未畀錢，公司派我去跑數。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 haak3 wu6 ci4 zo2 mei6 bei2 cin2, gung1 si1 paai3 ngo5 heoi3 paau2 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個客戶遲遲沒付錢，公司派我去催款。
examples.english_sentence: That client still hasn't paid; the company sent me to collect the payment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今個月跑咗幾多數？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 go3 jyut6 paau2 zo2 gei2 do1 sou3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這個月跑了多少客/多少單？
examples.english_sentence: How many accounts did you handle this month?

mandarin_meaning: 逃跑；溜走；不出现/避而不谈（口语）
english_meaning: to run off; to flee; to bail out / to not show up or avoid something (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，通常用來描述某人逃走、溜走、不出現或在敏感/麻煩情況下選擇避開。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe someone fleeing, running away, not showing up, or avoiding a sensitive/troublesome situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到差人，佢即刻跑晒山。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou6 caa1 jan4, keoi5 zik1 hak1 paau2 saai3 saan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到警察，他立刻逃跑了。
examples.english_sentence: When he saw the police, he immediately ran off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 討論到敏感話題，大家都跑晒山。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tou2 leon6 dou3 man5 gam2 waa6 tai4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 paau2 saai3 saan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一討論到敏感話題，大家就都回避/溜走了。
examples.english_sentence: When the sensitive topic came up, everyone bailed out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢答應會嚟幫手，但到時跑晒山，咩都無做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daap3 jing3 wui5 lai4 bong1 sau2, daan6 dou3 si4 paau2 saai3 saan1, me1 dou1 mou5 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他答应会来帮忙，但到时候却没出现，什么都没做。
examples.english_sentence: He promised to help, but didn't show up in the end and did nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 跑步
english_meaning: to run; to jog; running (as exercise)
explanation_mandarin: 指用雙腳快速移動，通常作為運動、鍛煉或競賽的一種行為。
explanation_english: The action of moving quickly on foot, commonly referring to running as exercise or in competition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝去跑步喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 heoi3 paau2 bou6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上去跑步了。
examples.english_sentence: I went for a run this morning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你鍾唔鍾意跑步？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 paau2 bou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你喜不喜歡跑步？
examples.english_sentence: Do you like running?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生建議我每日跑步三十分鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 gin3 ji3 ngo5 mui5 jat6 paau2 bou6 saam1 sap6 fan1 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 醫生建議我每天跑步三十分鐘。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor recommended I run 30 minutes every day.

mandarin_meaning: 跑步径 / 慢跑道
english_meaning: jogging path; running track (for jogging/running)
explanation_mandarin: 公园或户外供人慢跑或跑步使用的专用小道或跑道。
explanation_english: A path or track in parks or outdoor areas designated for jogging or running.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我成日喺公園嗰條跑步徑跑步，朝早空氣好清新。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gung1 jyun4 go2 tiu4 paau2 bou6 ging3 paau2 bou6, ziu1 zou2 hung1 hei3 hou2 cing1 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我经常在公园那条跑步径跑步，早上空气很清新。
examples.english_sentence: I often run on the jogging path in the park; the air is very fresh in the morning.

mandarin_meaning: 跑步機 / 跑步机 (pǎobùjī) — 室內用來跑步或走路的運動器械
english_meaning: treadmill (a machine for walking or running in place)
explanation_mandarin: 一種運動器械，通常有一條會轉動的跑帶，讓人在室內模擬跑步或快走，用於有氧運動或熱身。
explanation_english: A fitness machine with a moving belt that allows a person to walk or run in place, used for aerobic exercise, training, or warm-ups.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗一部跑步機，喺屋企可以做運動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 jat1 bou6 paau2 bou6 gei1, hai2 uk1 kei5 ho2 ji5 zou6 wan6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我買了一部跑步機，在家可以做運動。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a treadmill so I can exercise at home.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日去健身室會唔會用跑步機做熱身？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 heoi3 gin6 san1 sat1 wui5 m4 wui5 jung6 paau2 bou6 gei1 zou6 jit6 san1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天去健身房会不会用跑步机做热身？
examples.english_sentence: Are you going to use the treadmill to warm up at the gym today?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 跑步機壞咗，要叫人嚟維修。
examples.jyutping_sentence: paau2 bou6 gei1 waai6 zo2, jiu3 giu3 jan4 lai4 wai4 sau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 跑步机坏了，要叫人来维修。
examples.english_sentence: The treadmill is broken and needs someone to repair it.

mandarin_meaning: 接私人工作／接私活（通常指私下接的鐘點工作或兼職）
english_meaning: to take private gigs / moonlight (take on private/off‑the‑books shift work or appointments)
explanation_mandarin: 「跑私鐘」是香港粵語俗語，指私下接手或臨時承接的鐘點性工作或約會（例如私人補習、家務、按摩、陪診等），通常不是透過正式機構或未申報的兼職工作。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase meaning to take private/unscheduled gigs or shifts (e.g., private tutoring, home help, massage appointments), usually done off the record or outside formal employment channels.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚要去跑私鐘，替學生補習兩個鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 heoi3 paau2 si1 zung1, tai3 hok6 saang1 bou2 zaap6 loeng5 go3 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚要去做私人家教，給學生補習兩個小時。
examples.english_sentence: I have to go do a private tutoring gig tonight, tutoring a student for two hours.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫院話護士唔可以跑私鐘，會被紀律處分。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 jyun2 waa6 wu6 si6 m4 ho2 ji5 paau2 si1 zung1, wui5 bei6 gei2 leot6 cyu3 fan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 醫院說護士不可以接私人工作，會被紀律處分。
examples.english_sentence: The hospital says nurses cannot take private gigs; they'd be disciplined.

mandarin_meaning: 跑腿（跑腿、跑差、替人辦事）
english_meaning: to run errands; to do chores or deliver things on someone else's behalf
explanation_mandarin: 表示替人處理瑣碎的差事或代為送東西、辦事等。屬於口語常用詞，常用於請人幫忙外出辦事或受僱為他人跑單。
explanation_english: Refers to doing errands, small tasks, or deliveries for someone else. It is a colloquial term often used when someone is asked to go out and handle a task or work as a runner on behalf of others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家要出街幫佢跑腿，唔使等我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 jiu3 ceot1 gaai1 bong1 keoi5 paau2teoi2, m4 sai2 dang2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在要出門幫他跑腿，不用等我。
examples.english_sentence: I need to go out to run an errand for him now—don't wait for me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司叫我今晚替客戶跑腿，要送啲材料去佢哋辦公室。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1si1 giu3 ngo5 gam1maan5 tai3 haak3wu6 paau2teoi2, jiu3 sung3 di1 coi4liu6 heoi3 keoi5dei6 baan6gung1sat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司叫我今晚替客户跑腿，要送一些材料到他們辦公室。
examples.english_sentence: The company asked me to run an errand for a client tonight—to deliver some materials to their office.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日俾人搵去跑腿，人工又唔高。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4jat6 bei2 jan4 wan2 heoi3 paau2teoi2, jan4gung1 jau6 m4 gou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常被人叫去跑腿，工資又不高。
examples.english_sentence: He is often sent to run errands for people, and the pay isn't high.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）外出跑腿、在街上走動做事或拜訪客戶/逛街
english_meaning: to run errands; to go out and run around the streets (including doing outside business/visiting clients or casual shopping)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，指外出跑腿、在街上四處走動處理事情或做外勤、也可指出去逛街購物。
explanation_english: Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to go out to run errands or be out doing fieldwork/visiting clients; can also mean to go out and stroll/shop.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日要去跑街，可能夜啲先返到屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 paau2 gaai1, ho2 nang4 je6 di1 sin1 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天要出門跑腿，可能要晚一點才能回家。
examples.english_sentence: I have to run errands today; I might not get home until later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做保險要經常跑街見客。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 bou2 him2 jiu3 ging1 soeng4 paau2 gaai1 gin3 haak3.
