examples.english_sentence: He always blurts things out and interrupts; his speech is very impulsive.

mandarin_meaning: 張口結舌；一時說不出話來
english_meaning: to be tongue-tied; speechless; unable to speak because of surprise, nervousness, or embarrassment
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話說法，形容因驚訝、緊張或尷尬而說不出話或結巴。相當於普通話的「張口結舌」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is tongue-tied or speechless due to shock, nervousness, or embarrassment. Equivalent to Mandarin '張口結舌'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到偶像嘅時候，開口𤜯着脷，連一句都講唔出口。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 au2 zoeng6 ge3 si4 hau6, hoi1 hau2 waat6 zoek3 leoi6, lin4 jat1 geoi3 dou1 gong2 m4 ceot1 hau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他見到偶像時張口結舌，連一句話都說不出來。
examples.english_sentence: When he saw his idol, he was tongue-tied and couldn't even say a single sentence.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：張開嘴巴伸出舌頭；引申：因驚訝、困惑或傻愣而呆住、說不出話，或用以表示不屑/嘲弄。
english_meaning: Literal: open one's mouth and stick out one's tongue; Figurative: to be dumbfounded/stunned/speechless, or to show sulking/defiance/taunting.
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語可作字面理解（露出舌頭），亦常用作比喻，描述一個人因驚訝、困惑或無語而呆立，或用作嘲弄、撒嬌、鬧情緒的表現。注意其中字形（𤜯）為罕用字，讀音資料不一。
explanation_english: This colloquial expression can be taken literally (sticking out the tongue) or figuratively to describe someone who is stunned, speechless, sulking, or taunting. Note the character 𤜯 is rare and its pronunciation can be uncertain in some resources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嚇到開口𤜯著脷，唔識講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haak3 dou3 hoi1 hau2 [𤜯:unknown] zoek3 lep6, m4 sik1 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被嚇得張口伸出舌頭，說不出話。
examples.english_sentence: He was so shocked he opened his mouth and stuck out his tongue and couldn't speak.

mandarin_meaning: 翻舊帳／提舊事
english_meaning: to bring up old issues; to dredge up the past
explanation_mandarin: 「開古」是廣東話口語，常用於香港，意思是再次提起過去的事情或翻舊帳，通常帶有抱怨或指責的語氣。
explanation_english: “開古” is Cantonese slang (commonly used in Hong Kong) meaning to bring up past matters or dredge up old issues, often with a complaining or reproachful tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再開古，已經係好耐之前嘅事啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 hoi1 gu2, ji5 ging1 hai6 hou2 noi6 zi1 cin4 ge3 si6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要再翻舊帳，已經是很久以前的事了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't bring up old issues again; it's something from a long time ago.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意開古，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 hoi1 gu2, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是喜歡翻舊帳，弄得大家不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He always likes to bring up old matters, making everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: 開播；開始直播／開始廣播
english_meaning: to start broadcasting; to go live (start a livestream or a channel's broadcast)
explanation_mandarin: 在粵語口語及網絡語境中，「開台」多指主播或頻道開始直播（go live），也可指電視台／廣播頻道開始播出。
explanation_english: In Cantonese (especially slang/internet usage), '開台' means to start a broadcast — typically to go live on a streaming platform. It can also refer to a TV/radio channel beginning its scheduled broadcast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家開台，你哋上嚟撐我啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 toi4, nei5 dei6 soeng5 lai4 caang1 ngo5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在開播，你們上來支持我吧。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going live now — come support me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電視台喺早上八點開台。
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 si6 toi4 hai2 zou2 soeng6 baat3 dim2 hoi1 toi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 電視台在早上八點開播。
examples.english_sentence: The TV channel starts broadcasting at 8 AM.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開台之後，有好多觀眾捐咗禮物。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 toi4 zi1 hau6, jau5 hou2 do1 gwaan1 zung3 gyun3 zo2 lai5 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他開播之後，有很多觀眾送了禮物。
examples.english_sentence: After he went live, many viewers sent gifts.

mandarin_meaning: 登記姓名；報名、註冊（口語）
english_meaning: to register one's name; to sign up; to enroll (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「開名」為香港廣東話常用口語，指把姓名列入名單或進行報名／註冊。例如報名活動、登記出席或把人加入某個名單時可以說「開名」。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, '開名' is a colloquial verb meaning to register a name, sign up, or enroll—i.e., putting someone's name on a list for an event, account, attendance, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你開咗名未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hoi1 zo2 ming4 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你已經報名了嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Have you already signed up?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺網站上開名咗，等佢哋確認先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 mong5 zaam6 soeng6 hoi1 ming4 zo2, dang2 keoi5 dei6 kok3 jing6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在網站上已經登記了，等他們確認一下。
examples.english_sentence: I signed up on the website; waiting for them to confirm first.

mandarin_meaning: 开麦 / 开麦克风（打开麦克风、解除静音）
english_meaning: turn on the microphone; unmute; start speaking/broadcasting via mic
explanation_mandarin: 口語的廣東話用語，指把麥克風打開或在語音/直播中解除靜音，開始說話或播音。常見於直播、KTV、語音通話和線上會議等場景。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to switch on a microphone or unmute oneself in a voice chat or livestream; to start speaking or broadcasting. Commonly used in livestreaming, karaoke, voice calls, and online meetings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你開咪啦，我聽唔到你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hoi1 mai1 laa1, ngo5 teng1 m4 dou2 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你開麥啦，我聽不到你。
examples.english_sentence: Turn on your mic, I can't hear you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 錄影前記住開咪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: luk6 jing2 cin4 gei3 zyu6 hoi1 mai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 錄影前記得開麥。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to turn on the mic before recording.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺Zoom會議，如果你要講嘢就要開咪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 Zoom wui6 ji5, jyu4 gwo2 nei5 jiu3 gong2 je5 zau6 jiu3 hoi1 mai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在Zoom會議，如果你要講話就要開麥。
examples.english_sentence: In a Zoom meeting, if you want to speak you need to unmute/turn on your mic.

mandarin_meaning: 开启 / 开启（开始、打开）
english_meaning: to open; to start; to turn on; to enable
explanation_mandarin: 表示打開、啟動或開始某物或某個狀態，書面語常見，用於設備、功能或抽象概念（如人生新階段）的開始。
explanation_english: Indicates opening, starting, or enabling something; commonly used in written language for devices, features, or abstract concepts (e.g., starting a new chapter in life).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 請開啓部電腦，我要查啲電郵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cing2 hoi1 kai2 bou6 din6 nou5, ngo5 jiu3 caa4 di1 din6 jau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 请开启电脑，我要查一些电邮。
examples.english_sentence: Please turn on the computer; I need to check some emails.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開啓呢個功能之前要先登入先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 kai2 ni1 go3 gung1 nang4 zi1 cin4 jiu3 sin1 dang1 jap6 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开启这个功能之前要先登录才行。
examples.english_sentence: You need to log in before you can enable this feature.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近開啓咗人生新嘅一頁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 hoi1 kai2 zo2 jan4 sang1 san1 ge3 jat1 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近开启了人生新的一页。
examples.english_sentence: He has recently started a new chapter in his life.

mandarin_meaning: 开启
english_meaning: to open; to start; to initiate
explanation_mandarin: 表示打開、展開或開始某事或某物，常用於正式或書面語境。
explanation_english: Indicates opening, starting, or initiating something; often used in formal or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 請開啟電腦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cing2 hoi1 kai2 din6 nou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 请开启电脑。
examples.english_sentence: Please turn on the computer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 要開啟呢個檔案，你要有密碼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 hoi1 kai2 ni1 go3 dong2 on3, nei5 jiu3 jau5 mat6 maa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要开启这个档案，你需要有密码。
examples.english_sentence: To open this file, you need a password.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開啟新嘅計劃之前，我哋要討論預算。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 kai2 san1 ge3 gai3 waak6 zi1 cin4, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 tou2 leon6 jyu6 syun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在开启新的计划之前，我们要讨论预算。
examples.english_sentence: Before initiating the new project, we need to discuss the budget.

mandarin_meaning: 开启 / 打开 / 开始
english_meaning: to open; to start; to activate
explanation_mandarin: 表示打開某物或啟動、開始某個過程或狀態，既可指實體（如裝置、門窗），也可指抽象概念（如興趣、計畫）。
explanation_english: Indicates opening something or initiating/starting a process or state; can refer to physical objects (e.g., devices, doors) or abstract concepts (e.g., interest, projects).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋已經開啟咗新嘅專案，大家準備好未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji5 ging1 hoi1 kai2 zo2 san1 ge3 zyun1 on3, daai6 gaa1 zeon2 bei6 hou2 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們已經開啟了新的專案，大家準備好了嗎？
examples.english_sentence: We've already started the new project; is everyone ready?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 請按呢個掣開啟電腦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cing2 on3 ni1 go3 zai3 hoi1 kai2 din6 nou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 請按這個按鈕開啟電腦。
examples.english_sentence: Please press this button to start the computer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本書開啟咗我對歷史嘅興趣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 syu1 hoi1 kai2 zo2 ngo5 deoi3 lik6 si2 ge3 hing3 ceoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這本書開啟了我對歷史的興趣。
examples.english_sentence: This book opened my interest in history.

mandarin_meaning: 开善堂；慈善组织或善堂，提供救济、赈济、教育或丧葬等慈善服务的机构
english_meaning: a charitable hall; a philanthropic organization or benevolent society that provides relief, social services, or charitable activities
explanation_mandarin: 指由社群或宗族设立的慈善机构或善堂，通常用于救济穷困、办学、设立义诊或处理丧葬等公益事务，在粤港地区历史上较常见。
explanation_english: Refers to a charitable organization or benevolent hall, often established by a community or lineage to provide aid to the poor, run schools, free clinics, or handle funeral relief; historically common in Cantonese-speaking regions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋村入面有間開善堂，成日幫助貧困嘅人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 cyun1 jap6 min6 jau5 gaan1 hoi1 sin6 tong4, sing4 jat6 bong1 zo6 pan4 kwan3 ge3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们村里有家开善堂，经常帮助贫困的人。
examples.english_sentence: There's a charitable hall in our village that often helps people in poverty.

mandarin_meaning: 開嗓 / 清嗓 / 首次演唱
english_meaning: to open one's voice / to warm up the voice; to sing the opening song or perform the first vocal piece; to clear one's throat
explanation_mandarin: 「開喉」是廣東話口語，字面上是「打開喉嚨」。常用來表示為唱歌或公開發言而清嗓、暖嗓、做聲音準備；在KTV或演出場合也用作「唱第一首歌／開場演唱」的意思。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開喉' (literally 'open the throat') is an informal expression meaning to clear or warm up the voice for singing or speaking. It can also mean to sing the opening song or be the opening performer at an event.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去K房，你可唔可以幫我開喉？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 K fong2, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 hau4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去KTV，你能不能幫我開嗓？
examples.english_sentence: We're going to KTV tonight — can you sing the opening song for me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上台之前我要開喉暖聲，避免走音。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng5 toi4 zi1 cin4 ngo5 jiu3 hoi1 hau4 nyun5 sing1, bei6 min5 zau2 jam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上台之前我要開嗓暖聲，避免走音。
examples.english_sentence: I need to warm up my voice before going on stage to avoid going off-key.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢前先開喉，好似有重要嘅宣佈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 cin4 sin1 hoi1 hau4, hou2 ci5 jau5 zung6 jiu3 ge3 syun1 bou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他讲话前先清嗓，好像有重要的宣佈。
examples.english_sentence: He cleared his throat before speaking — it seems like he has an important announcement.

mandarin_meaning: 开单 / 开发票 / 开罚单（视情境而定）
english_meaning: to issue a bill/invoice/ticket (e.g., a restaurant bill, invoice, or traffic/parking fine)
explanation_mandarin: 「開單」在廣東話中常用作動詞，根據情境可以指：餐廳或商戶出帳單或賬單、公司開發票，或警方/有關部門開罰單（處罰或罰款）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "開單" is a verb meaning to issue a bill/invoice or a ticket. Depending on context, it can refer to preparing a restaurant bill, issuing an invoice to a client, or issuing a fine/penalty (e.g., parking or traffic ticket).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋會幫你開單。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 wui5 bong1 nei5 hoi1 daan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們會幫你開單。
examples.english_sentence: We'll prepare the bill for you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警察對佢開單，因為佢泊車違例。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 caat3 deoi3 keoi5 hoi1 daan1, jan1 wai6 keoi5 paak3 ce1 wai4 lai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警察對他開了罰單，因為他違規停車。
examples.english_sentence: The police issued him a ticket because he parked illegally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要開單畀客戶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 hoi1 daan1 bei2 haak3 wu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要給客戶開發票。
examples.english_sentence: The company needs to issue an invoice to the client.

mandarin_meaning: 開始（開始做某事）
english_meaning: to start to; to begin to (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 「開嚟」是廣東話口語用法，通常表示開始做某事或突然開始某個動作，常與動詞連用。有時亦可用來表示動作朝說話者方向（此用法較少見）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to start or begin doing something, often used with a verb. It can also sometimes imply an action toward the speaker, though that use is less common.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開嚟喊，原來係因為啲事搞唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 lai4 haam3, jyun4 loi4 hai6 jan1 wai6 di1 si6 gaau2 m4 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他開始哭了，原來是因為有些事情處理不來。
examples.english_sentence: He started crying — it turned out it was because he couldn't handle some matters.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）開始擲骰子；（引申）開始做冒險或挑起事端、賭一把
english_meaning: Literally 'start rolling the dice' (to begin gambling); figuratively, to take a risky action or provoke trouble that may affect others.
explanation_mandarin: 「開圍骰」原指開始擲骰子、開賭局；在香港粵語口語中常引申為做一個冒險決定或挑起事端，可能會牽連其他人。
explanation_english: Originally refers to starting to roll dice or opening a gambling round. In Hong Kong Cantonese it is often used figuratively to mean taking a risky gamble or provoking trouble that could involve others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好開圍骰，會牽連晒啲人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hoi1 wai4 suk6, wui5 hin1 lin4 saai3 di1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別開圍骰，會牽連到其他人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't start this gamble/trouble — it will drag other people in.

mandarin_meaning: 發起團購或組織一個團體活動
english_meaning: to start/organize a group (e.g., a group-buy or a group activity/party)
explanation_mandarin: 「開團」是粵語口語用法，通常指發起團購、組團下單或組織多人一同參與某項活動，例如團購、代購、或打遊戲副本等。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, '開團' means to start or organize a group — commonly used for initiating group-buys (group orders) or assembling people for a joint activity (e.g., group purchase, group order, or a gaming party/raid).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我打算開團買日本零食，大家有興趣嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 daa2 syun3 hoi1 tyun4 maai5 jat6 bun2 ling4 sik6, daai6 gaa1 jau5 hing3 ceoi3 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我打算發起團購買日本零食，大家有興趣嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I'm planning to start a group buy for Japanese snacks — is anyone interested?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次開團係為咗公司年尾買禮物，記得報名喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 hoi1 tyun4 hai6 wai6 zo2 gung1 si1 nin4 mei5 maai5 lai5 mat6, gei3 dak1 bou3 ming4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次我發起團購是為了公司年末買禮物，記得報名。
examples.english_sentence: This time we're organizing a group buy to buy company year-end gifts — remember to sign up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚開團打副本，七點喺Discord集合。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 hoi1 tyun4 daa2 fu3 bun2, cat1 dim2 hai2 Discord zip3 hap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚組團打副本，七點在Discord集合。
examples.english_sentence: We're forming a party to run the dungeon tonight; meet on Discord at 7.

mandarin_meaning: （網絡/口語）開一個新項目/開帖/開位；有時也指設陷阱、坑騙別人
english_meaning: to open/start a new project/slot/thread (online or creative); occasionally to set a trap or trick someone
explanation_mandarin: 在香港粵語網絡或口語中，"開坑"常用來表示開始一個新項目、開一個帖/位讓人加入或後續發展；另有用法指設陷阱、坑騙別人，語氣偏向俚語或次文化用語。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese internet/colloquial use, "開坑" often means to start a new project, open a thread/slot for others to join, or begin a series; it can also mean to set a trap or deceive someone. It is slangy and common in online communities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱開咗個新坑，打算寫一個短篇系列，邊個想加入？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aam1 aam1 hoi1 zo2 go3 san1 haang1, daa2 syun3 se2 jat1 go3 dyun2 pin1 hai6 lit6, bin1 go3 soeng2 gaa1 jap6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我刚刚开了一个新坑，打算写一个短篇系列，谁想加入？
examples.english_sentence: I just opened a new project/slot and plan to write a short-series — who wants to join?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個人成日坑人，千祈唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 jan4 sing4 jat6 haang1 jan4, cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个人经常坑别人，千万不要相信他。
examples.english_sentence: That person often tricks people — don't trust him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家開緊坑，等緊人入隊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 gan2 haang1, dang2 gan2 jan4 jap6 deoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我现在正在开坑，等人加入队伍。
examples.english_sentence: I'm opening a slot now, waiting for people to join the team.

jyutping: hoi1 maai4 zeng2 gwo3 jan4 sik6 seoi2
mandarin_meaning: 做了準備或付出努力，最後讓別人享受成果／得利（含被佔便宜、不公平之意）
english_meaning: To do the work or make the preparations but let others reap the benefits (implies being taken advantage of or an unfair outcome)
explanation_mandarin: 指辛苦做事或準備，最後成果卻讓別人享用或佔去，通常帶有被佔便宜或不公平的涵義。
explanation_english: Refers to putting in the hard work or making preparations only to have others enjoy the results; usually implies being taken advantage of or an unfair situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋辛辛苦苦做晒啲準備，佢嚟到就開埋井過人食水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 san1 san1 fu2 fu2 zou6 saai3 di1 zeon2 bei6, keoi5 loi4 dou3 zau6 hoi1 maai4 zeng2 gwo3 jan4 sik6 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們辛辛苦苦做了準備，他一來就把成果讓別人享用。
examples.english_sentence: We worked hard preparing everything, and when he arrived he let others reap the benefits.

mandarin_meaning: 結帳、結算（帳目）
english_meaning: to settle accounts / to pay the bill; to settle up
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示把帳目結清或結帳；也可以泛指把事情或欠款了結、算清楚。常用於餐廳結帳或朋友之間分攤錢款時。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to settle accounts or pay the bill; can also mean to settle up or clear outstanding matters. Commonly used when splitting a bill or clearing debts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋食咗飯就開埋數啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sik6 zo2 faan6 zau6 hoi1 maai4 sou3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們吃完飯就結帳吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's settle the bill after we finish eating.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚記得同佢開埋數，唔好留尾數。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 gei3 dak1 tung4 keoi5 hoi1 maai4 sou3, m4 hou2 lau4 mei5 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚記得跟他把帳結清，不要留下尾款。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to settle the account with him tonight; don't leave any outstanding balance.

mandarin_meaning: 開埠 (kāibù)：開放港口／城市以進行對外通商，或指一個地區開始作為對外貿易的港口而發展。
english_meaning: to open a port; to open a city/area to foreign trade; to establish a trading port
explanation_mandarin: 指使某地開放港口或通商，通常用於歷史或地理語境，描述一個地方開始成為對外貿易的港口或商埠。
explanation_english: Refers to opening a port or opening an area to external trade. Commonly used in historical or geographical contexts to describe when a place becomes a trading port.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港喺1842年開埠，之後發展成為國際貿易中心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 hai2 jat1 baat3 sei3 ji6 nin4 hoi1 fau6, zi1 hau6 faat3 zin2 sing4 wai4 gwok3 zai3 mau6 jik6 zung1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港在1842年開埠，之後發展成為國際貿易中心。
examples.english_sentence: Hong Kong opened as a port in 1842 and later developed into an international trade center.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個漁村以前冇開埠，只係細小嘅社區。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 jyu4 cyun1 ji5 cin4 mou5 hoi1 fau6, zi2 hai6 sai3 siu2 ge3 se5 keoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個漁村以前沒有開埠，只是個小社區。
examples.english_sentence: This fishing village didn't open as a port before; it was just a small community.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府計劃喺沿海新城開埠，吸引外國商人投資。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gai3 waak6 hai2 jin4 hoi2 san1 sing4 hoi1 fau6, kap1 jan5 ngoi6 gwok3 soeng1 jan4 tau4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府計劃在沿海新城開埠，吸引外國商人投資。
examples.english_sentence: The government plans to open a port in the new coastal city to attract foreign merchants and investment.

mandarin_meaning: 开场；开幕；开始（演出、活动的开始部分或开头）
english_meaning: opening; to open (a performance/event); opening scene/remarks
explanation_mandarin: 「開場」可作動詞，表示（演出、活動等）開始；亦可作名詞，指開頭的部分，如開場白、開場戲或開幕儀式。
explanation_english: “開場” can be a verb meaning to start or open (a performance or event), and a noun referring to the opening part (e.g., opening remarks, opening scene, or opening ceremony).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開場前五分鐘，大家要就位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 coeng4 cin4 ng5 fan1 zung1, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zau6 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开场前五分钟，大家要就位。
examples.english_sentence: Five minutes before the opening, everyone should take their positions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺開場時講咗一段開場白。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 hoi1 coeng4 si4 gong2 zo2 jat1 dyun6 hoi1 coeng4 baak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在开场时说了一段开场白。
examples.english_sentence: He gave an opening speech at the start.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開場戲好重要，要吸引觀眾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 coeng4 hei3 hou2 zung6 jiu3, jiu3 kap1 jan5 gun1 zung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开场戏很重要，要吸引观众。
examples.english_sentence: The opening scene is very important; it needs to captivate the audience.

mandarin_meaning: 开场白
english_meaning: opening remarks; introductory words
explanation_mandarin: 指在活動、演講或會議開始時所說的引言或致詞，用來介紹主題、吸引聽眾或設定氣氛。
explanation_english: Refers to the introductory words or remarks given at the start of an event, speech, or meeting, used to introduce the topic, engage the audience, or set the tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺會議開頭講咗一段好有力嘅開場白。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 wui6 ji5 hoi1 tau4 gong2 zo2 jat1 dyun6 hou2 jau5 lik6 ge3 hoi1 coeng4 baak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在会议一开始就讲了一段很有力的开场白。
examples.english_sentence: He delivered a very powerful opening remark at the beginning of the meeting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 主持人用輕鬆嘅開場白引導觀眾進入主題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zyu2 ci4 jan4 jung6 hing1 sung1 ge3 hoi1 coeng4 baak6 jan5 dou6 gun1 zung3 zeon3 jap6 zyu2 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 主持人用轻松的开场白引导观众进入主题。
examples.english_sentence: The host used a light-hearted opening remark to lead the audience into the topic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好拖長開場白，直接講重點啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 to1 coeng4 hoi1 coeng4 baak6, zik6 zip3 gong2 zung6 dim2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要把开场白讲得太长，直接说明重点吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't drag out the opening remarks; get straight to the point.

mandarin_meaning: 开垦
english_meaning: to reclaim (land); to clear and cultivate (previously uncultivated land)
explanation_mandarin: 把荒地或未開發的土地整理、開拓並開始耕種，使其可以用來種植或利用。
explanation_english: To prepare and convert unused or wild land for cultivation or productive use; clearing and cultivating land that was previously uncultivated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋打算開墾嗰塊荒地，種菜同埋果樹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 daa2 syun3 hoi1 kon2 go2 faai3 fong1 dei6, zung2 coi3 tung4 maai4 gwo2 syu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們打算開墾那塊荒地，種菜和果樹。
examples.english_sentence: They plan to reclaim that plot of wasteland to plant vegetables and fruit trees.

mandarin_meaning: 香港罕見俗語，來源不明，泛指某種機器或裝置；有時被猜測為英語借詞的音譯（例如 kiosk 或 cashier），但沒有確定來源。
english_meaning: A rare/obscure Hong Kong Cantonese slang term referring to some kind of machine or device. Origin is unclear; sometimes conjectured to be a phonetic loan from English (e.g., 'kiosk' or 'cashier'), but not established.
explanation_mandarin: 「開士機」在粵語中屬於罕見或地方性俗語，沒有統一或正式的詞源說法。使用時通常指某台機器或裝置，具體指涉需看語境。
explanation_english: Used as a rare/local Cantonese slang noun for a machine or device. There is no agreed etymology; meaning is context-dependent and may reflect a phonetic borrowing from English, but this is uncertain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔識用嗰部開士機，你可唔可以教我？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik1 jung6 go2 bou6 hoi1 si6 gei1, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gaau3 ngo5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不會用那台「開士機」，你可以教我嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I don't know how to use that 'hoi si gei' machine. Can you teach me?

mandarin_meaning: 通宵／熬夜（或值夜班，視語境而定）
english_meaning: to stay up late / pull an all-nighter; (contextually) to work a night shift
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話口語中，「開夜」常用來表示熬夜或通宵做某事（例如讀書、玩樂、打機），有時也用來表示在夜間值班或上夜班，具體含義視語境而定。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial speech, "開夜" commonly means to stay up late or pull an all-nighter (e.g., for studying, partying, or gaming). It can also mean working a night shift; the exact meaning depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋唔好開夜啦，聽日要返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 m4 hou2 hoi1 je6 laa1, ting1 jat6 jiu3 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們今晚不要熬夜了，明天要上班。
examples.english_sentence: Let's not stay up late tonight; we have to go to work tomorrow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我成日為功課開夜，宜家好攰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 wai6 gung1 fo3 hoi1 je6, ji4 gaa1 hou2 gui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我常常為了功課熬夜，現在很累。
examples.english_sentence: I often pull all-nighters for homework; I'm really tired now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今晚要喺醫院開夜，唔可以一齊出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 hai2 ji1 jyun2 hoi1 je6, m4 ho2 ji5 jat1 cai4 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今晚要在醫院值夜班，不能一起出去。
examples.english_sentence: He has to work the night shift at the hospital tonight, so he can't go out with us.

mandarin_meaning: 熬夜；通宵工作或學習
english_meaning: to pull an all-nighter; stay up late working or studying
explanation_mandarin: 「開夜車」是粵語俗語，指為了趕工、趕交或溫習而通宵工作或讀書，熬夜到很晚。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to stay up late or pull an all-nighter, typically to work or study in order to meet a deadline or finish tasks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚要開夜車溫書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 hoi1 je6 ce1 wan1 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚得熬夜复习。
examples.english_sentence: I have to pull an all-nighter studying tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗趕交稿，佢連續幾晚開夜車。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 gon2 gaau1 gou2, keoi5 lin4 zuk6 gei2 maan5 hoi1 je6 ce1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了赶交稿，他连续好几晚熬夜。
examples.english_sentence: To meet the submission, he pulled all-nighters for several nights.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日開夜車，身體會受唔住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 hoi1 je6 ce1, san1 tai2 wui5 sau6 m4 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要总是熬夜，身体会吃不消。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep pulling all-nighters; your body won't be able to take it.

mandarin_meaning: 把（音量/強度/力度）開大；全力以赴、放手去做（口語）
english_meaning: to turn up to maximum (volume/power/intensity); (informal) to go all out / give maximum effort
explanation_mandarin: 「開大」在廣東話中常用作口語，表示把聲音、燈光、馬力等調到更大或最大；也可以引申為全力以赴、放手一搏、加大力度去做某事。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開大' is an informal expression meaning to increase something (volume, light, power) to a larger or maximum level; it can also be used figuratively to mean going all out or putting in maximum effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你把聲開大啲啦，我聽唔到你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 baa2 seng1 hoi1 daai6 di1 laa1, ngo5 teng1 m4 dou3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你把声音开大点，我听不到你。
examples.english_sentence: Turn up your volume a bit—I can't hear you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 把音響開大啲，我哋要跳舞！
examples.jyutping_sentence: baa2 jam1 hoeng2 hoi1 daai6 di1, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 tiu3 mou5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 把音响开大一点，我们要跳舞！
examples.english_sentence: Turn up the speakers, we're going to dance!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今場比賽佢開大喇，完全唔留手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 coeng4 bei2 coi3 keoi5 hoi1 daai6 laa3, jyun4 cyun4 m4 lau4 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这场比赛他全力以赴，完全不留手。
examples.english_sentence: He went all out in this match—no holding back.

mandarin_meaning: 誇張地表現／擺闊、做大場面（字面：拍攝大型電影）
english_meaning: to make a big show; to show off extravagantly; to put on a big spectacle (literally: shoot a blockbuster)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，字面上是「開大片」（拍攝大型電影），引申為誇張地表現、擺闊或製造大場面，常帶有貶義或嘲諷意味。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang. Literally 'to shoot a blockbuster', but used figuratively to mean behaving ostentatiously, showing off, or making a big production. Often carries a negative or mocking tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度開大片，冇必要咁誇張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 hoi1 daai6 pin3, mou5 bit1 jiu3 gam2 kwaa1 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在這裡誇張地表現，沒有必要那麼張揚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make a big show here; it's unnecessary to be so dramatic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺個聚會一邊開大片一邊扮嘢，想吸引注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 go3 zeoi6 wui6 jat1 bin1 hoi1 daai6 pin3 jat1 bin1 baan6 je5, soeng2 kap1 jan5 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在聚會上一邊誇張表現、一邊裝腔作勢，想吸引注意。
examples.english_sentence: He was making a big show and acting up at the party to attract attention.

jyutping: hoi1 tin1 saat3 gaa3 lok6 dei6 waan4 cin2
mandarin_meaning: （粵語俗語）先以極低價或誇張優惠吸引顧客，但在實際成交或兌現時出現各種限制、退回或不兌現的做法；亦可指大吹大擂、最後反悔或不負責任地收場。
english_meaning: A Cantonese colloquial phrase describing a tactic or behavior where outrageously low prices or flashy promotions are advertised to lure people, but when it comes to actual fulfillment there are hidden conditions, refunds, or no real delivery; it can also mean grand promises that are later reneged on.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容商家或個人以誇張的低價或優惠作招徠，但落實時卻有各種附加條件、退款或不履行承諾，實際情況與宣傳不符，帶有貶意。
explanation_english: Used to describe sellers or individuals who lure customers with exaggerated low prices or flashy deals, but when the deal is finalized there are hidden conditions, refunds, or failure to deliver—i.e., the reality does not match the promotion. It carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲優惠好多時係開天殺價落地還錢，睇落抵，但到手就唔係咁簡單。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ne1 di1 jau1 wai6 hou2 do1 si4 hai6 hoi1 tin1 saat3 gaa3 lok6 dei6 waan4 cin2, tai2 lok6 dai2, daan6 dou3 sau2 zau6 m4 hai6 gam2 gaan2 daan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些优惠很多时候是开天杀价落地还钱，看起来划算，但实际到手并不那么简单。
examples.english_sentence: These promotions are often 'open-the-sky slash prices, refund upon landing'—they look cheap at first, but when you actually get them it's not that simple.

mandarin_meaning: 放鴿子；爽約
english_meaning: to stand someone up; to fail to show up for an appointment or cancel at the last minute without notice
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俗語，指在約定的時間不出現或臨時爽約，相當於普通話的「放鴿子／放飛機」。也可用於指廣播或節目臨時停播、取消排期。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese idiom/slang meaning to fail to show up for an appointment (to stand someone up) or to cancel/skip a scheduled event without prior notice. It can also be used for broadcasts or programs that are suddenly not aired.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日約咗我食飯，結果開天窗，我好失望。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 joek3 zo2 ngo5 sik6 faan6, git3 gwo2 hoi1 tin1 coeng1, ngo5 hou2 sat1 mong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天約我吃飯，結果放鴿子，我很失望。
examples.english_sentence: He arranged to meet me for lunch today but stood me up; I'm very disappointed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電台今日開天窗，冇播原定嘅節目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 toi4 gam1 jat6 hoi1 tin1 coeng1, mou5 bo3 jyun4 ding6 ge3 zit3 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 電台今天取消了原定的節目，臨時停播。
examples.english_sentence: The radio station cancelled the scheduled program today and didn't broadcast the planned show.

mandarin_meaning: 漫天要价；索取天价
english_meaning: to demand exorbitant prices; to ask for the moon
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，形容收取或要求極高、離譜的價格，通常帶有批評或不滿的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to describe demanding extremely high or outrageous prices; usually conveys criticism or dissatisfaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間舖開天索價，實在買唔落手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 hoi1 tin1 sok3 gaa3, sat6 zoi6 maai5 m4 lok6 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間店漫天要價，實在買不下手。
examples.english_sentence: This shop is asking outrageous prices; I can't bring myself to buy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個供應商成日開天索價，冇人想同佢做生意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 gung1 jing3 soeng1 sing4 jat6 hoi1 tin1 sok3 gaa3, mou5 jan4 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 zou6 sang1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個供應商總是漫天要價，沒人願意跟他做生意。
examples.english_sentence: That supplier constantly demands exorbitant prices; nobody wants to do business with him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間屋裝修報價遠超預算，簡直係開天索價。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 uk1 zong1 sau1 bou3 gaa3 jyun5 ciu1 jyu6 syun3, gaan2 zik6 hai6 hoi1 tin1 sok3 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 房子的裝修報價遠超預算，簡直是漫天要價。
examples.english_sentence: The renovation quote for the house far exceeds the budget—it's practically asking for the moon.

jyutping: hoi1 tin1 sok3 gaa3 lok6 dei6 waan4 cin2
mandarin_meaning: 起初開出天價或提出不切實際的條件，最後回到現實、退還多餘或改為合理價格
english_meaning: To demand a sky-high price or make extravagant demands at first, but then come back down to earth and refund the excess or settle for a realistic amount
explanation_mandarin: 形容有人或商家一開始開出極高或不切實際的價格或條件，但經過談判或現實情況後又退讓、給折扣或只收合理價錢。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where someone or a seller initially quotes an exorbitant price or sets unrealistic terms, but after negotiation or reality check they relent—offering discounts, refunds, or accepting a fairer amount.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間裝修公司一開始開天索價落地還錢，先報超貴嘅價，傾掂又俾返折，最後其實唔使咁多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 zong1 sau1 gung1 si1 jat1 hoi1 ci2 hoi1 tin1 sok3 gaa3 lok6 dei6 waan4 cin2, sin1 bou3 ciu1 gwai3 ge3 gaa3, king1 dim6 jau6 bei2 faan1 zit3, zeoi3 hau6 kei4 sat6 m4 sai2 gam3 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間裝修公司一開始報的是天價，但談妥後又給了折扣，最後其實不需要那麼多錢。
examples.english_sentence: That renovation company initially quoted a sky-high price, but after negotiations gave discounts and in the end it didn't cost that much.

mandarin_meaning: 开天辟地（成语）：原指创世，后用以形容开创了全新的局面或具有划时代意义的重大作为。
english_meaning: To create heaven and earth (idiom); figuratively, groundbreaking or epoch-making — to inaugurate a wholly new era or undertaking.
explanation_mandarin: 原指創造天地，後來引申為開創前所未有的新局面或重大成就，具有劃時代、開創性的含義。
explanation_english: Originally refers to the act of creating heaven and earth; figuratively used to describe something that is unprecedented and groundbreaking, marking the start of a new era or major achievement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢項發明真係開天闢地，改變咗成個行業。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 hong6 faat3 ming4 zan1 hai6 hoi1 tin1 pik1 dei6, goi2 bin3 zo2 seng4 go3 hong4 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這項發明真是開天辟地，改變了整個行業。
examples.english_sentence: This invention is truly groundbreaking; it changed the whole industry.

mandarin_meaning: （開始）泡/做奶茶；開奶茶店
english_meaning: to start/make milk tea; to open a milk-tea shop
explanation_mandarin: 粵語用語，字面意思是「開始做/泡奶茶」。可指在家或茶餐廳、檔口製作奶茶，也可指開設奶茶店或開始賣奶茶。
explanation_english: A Cantonese phrase literally meaning "to start/make milk tea." It can refer to brewing/making milk tea at home or in a cafe/stall, or to opening/starting a milk-tea shop/business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺屋企自己開奶茶，味道好正。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 uk1 kei2 zi6 gei2 hoi1 naai5 caa4, mei6 dou6 hou2 zeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在家自己泡奶茶，味道很好。
examples.english_sentence: He makes milk tea at home himself; it tastes great.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 茶餐廳一開門，師傅就開始開奶茶，客人即刻買。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caa4 caan1 teng1 jat1 hoi1 mun4, si1 fu1 zau6 hoi1 ci2 hoi1 naai5 caa4, haak3 jan4 zik1 hak1 maai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 茶餐厅一开门，师傅就开始泡奶茶，客人立刻就买。
examples.english_sentence: When the cha chaan teng opens, the cook starts making milk tea and customers buy it immediately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打算開間奶茶舖，下個月正式開業。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 syun3 hoi1 gaan1 naai5 caa4 pou3, haa6 go3 jyut6 zing3 sik1 hoi1 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打算开一家奶茶店，下个月正式开业。
examples.english_sentence: He plans to open a milk-tea shop; it will officially open next month.

mandarin_meaning: 开始
english_meaning: to begin; to start
explanation_mandarin: 表示某件事或动作的起始，用來說明開始一個活動、過程或狀態。
explanation_english: Indicates the beginning of an action, event, or process; used to say that something is starting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋而家開始啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 ci2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们现在开始吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's start now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開始學廣東話喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 ci2 hok6 gwong2 dung1 waa2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他开始学广东话了。
examples.english_sentence: He has started learning Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 課堂會喺九點開始。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fo3 tong4 wui5 hai2 gau2 dim2 hoi1 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 课堂会在九点开始。
examples.english_sentence: The class will start at nine o'clock.

mandarin_meaning: 开学（开始上课；学期开始）
english_meaning: to start school / the start of a school term; classes resume
explanation_mandarin: 表示學校開始上課或學期的開始，可作動詞（開學）或名詞（開學日）。
explanation_english: Refers to the start of classes or the beginning of a school term. Can be used as a verb (to start school) or as a noun (the start of term).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日開學，我要買書同文具。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 hoi1hok6, ngo5 jiu3 maai5 syu1 tung4 man4 geoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天开学，我要买书和文具。
examples.english_sentence: School starts tomorrow; I need to buy books and stationery.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開學第一日，學生好多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1hok6 dai6 jat6, hok6saang1 hou2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开学第一天，学生很多。
examples.english_sentence: On the first day of school there are many students.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 暑假完咗，禮拜一開學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: syu2 gaa3 jyun4 zo2, lai5 baai3 jat1 hoi1hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 暑假结束，星期一开学。
examples.english_sentence: The summer holiday is over; school starts on Monday.

mandarin_meaning: 开学典礼 / 开学礼
english_meaning: school opening ceremony; opening ceremony for the new school term/semester
explanation_mandarin: 指學校在新學期開始時舉行的儀式或典禮，通常包含校長致辭、介紹新老師或安排活動等。
explanation_english: Refers to a ceremony held by a school at the start of a new term, typically including speeches by the principal, introductions of staff, and related activities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學校下星期一有開學禮，大家要準時返學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 haau6 haa6 sing1 kei4 jat1 jau5 hoi1 hok6 lei5, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zeon2 si4 faan1 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学校下星期一有开学典礼，大家要准时上学。
examples.english_sentence: The school has an opening ceremony next Monday; everyone should arrive on time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 家長都好關心開學禮嘅安排，同埋有冇家長會環節。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaa1 zoeng2 dou1 hou2 gwaan1 sam1 hoi1 hok6 lei5 ge3 ngon1 paai4, tung4 maai4 jau5 mou5 gaa1 zoeng2 wui6 waan4 zit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家长们都很关心开学典礼的安排，以及是否有家长会环节。
examples.english_sentence: Parents are concerned about the opening ceremony arrangements and whether there will be a parents' meeting segment.

mandarin_meaning: 开宗明义：一开始就把宗旨、目的或要点讲清楚，直截了当地说明来意。
english_meaning: To state the purpose or main point clearly at the outset; to come straight to the point.
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示在一開始就把重點、目的或立場講明白，不拐彎抹角。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that one makes the main point, purpose, or stance clear from the beginning without beating around the bush.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開宗明義，我哋呢個計劃係為咗提升品牌形象。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 zung1 ming4 ji6, ngo5 dei6 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 hai6 wai6 zo2 tai4 sing1 pan2 paai4 jing4 zoeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开宗明义，我们这个计划是为了提升品牌形象。
examples.english_sentence: To be upfront, our plan is to improve the brand image.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆開宗明義講，新制度係為咗減低成本。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 hoi1 zung1 ming4 ji6 gong2, san1 zai3 dou6 hai6 wai6 zo2 gaam2 dai1 sing4 bun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板开宗明义地说，新制度是为了降低成本。
examples.english_sentence: The boss stated upfront that the new system is intended to reduce costs.

mandarin_meaning: 開庭審理 / 開審（開始審判）
english_meaning: to begin a trial; to open a court hearing
explanation_mandarin: 指法院開始對某宗案件進行審理、開庭審判的動作或程序。
explanation_english: Refers to the court starting to hear a case — the commencement of a trial or judicial hearing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件案聽日喺高等法院開審。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 on3 ting1 jat6 hai2 gou1 dang2 faat3 jyun6 hoi1 sam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這宗案子明天在高等法院開審。
examples.english_sentence: The case will go to trial at the High Court tomorrow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 律師話個案要到下個月先開審，仲要傳召幾個證人出庭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: leot6 si1 waa6 go3 on3 jiu3 dou3 haa6 go3 jyut6 sin1 hoi1 sam2, zung6 jiu3 cyun4 ziu1 gei2 go3 zing3 jan4 ceot1 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 律師說這宗案要等到下個月才開審，還要傳召幾個證人出庭。
examples.english_sentence: The lawyer said the case won't be tried until next month, and several witnesses still need to be summoned.

mandarin_meaning: 打开（信件、包裹等的封口）；（地名）开封（河南省的一座城市）
english_meaning: to open (a seal, envelope, or package); Kaifeng (a city in Henan, China)
explanation_mandarin: 表示拆开或打开封口，常用于信件、包裹等；另外“开封”也是河南省的一个地名。
explanation_english: Refers to opening a seal or unsealing something like a letter or package; also the name of a city (Kaifeng) in Henan province.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢封信未開封過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fung1 seon3 mei6 hoi1 fung1 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这封信没有被打开过。
examples.english_sentence: This letter hasn't been opened.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等我先開封個包裹睇下入面有咩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 sin1 hoi1 fung1 go3 baau1 gwo2 tai2 haa5 jap6 min6 jau5 me1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等我先打开这个包裹看看里面有什么。
examples.english_sentence: Let me open the package first to see what's inside.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開封係河南嘅一座歷史名城。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 fung1 hai6 Hon4 naam4 ge3 jat1 zo6 lik6 si2 ming4 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开封是河南的一座历史名城。
examples.english_sentence: Kaifeng is a historic city in Henan.

mandarin_meaning: 开导（给予劝导或疏导，使人理解或释怀）
english_meaning: to enlighten; to counsel; to advise or comfort someone so they can understand or feel better
explanation_mandarin: 表示用言语或事例引导、劝导别人，使其理解问题、释怀或改变态度。
explanation_english: To use words, examples, or guidance to help someone understand a situation, be comforted, or change their perspective.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我試過想開導佢，但佢唔聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 si3 gwo3 soeng2 hoi1 dou6 keoi5, daan6 keoi5 m4 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我曾经想开导他，但他不听。
examples.english_sentence: I tried to counsel him, but he wouldn't listen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老師用例子去開導學生，幫佢哋明白道理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 si1 jung6 lai6 zi2 heoi3 hoi1 dou6 hok6 saang1, bong1 keoi5 dei6 ming4 baak6 dou6 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老师用例子去开导学生，帮助他们明白道理。
examples.english_sentence: The teacher used examples to guide the students and help them understand the reasoning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢需要人開導，幫佢釐清自己嘅諗法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 jiu3 jan4 hoi1 dou6, bong1 keoi5 lei4 cing1 zi6 gei2 ge3 nam2 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他需要有人开导，帮他厘清自己的想法。
examples.english_sentence: He needs someone to talk to so they can help him sort out his thoughts.

mandarin_meaning: 开局；开始（比赛、对弈或事情的起始阶段）
english_meaning: opening; to begin/start (a game, match, or the initial stage of an event)
explanation_mandarin: 表示开始或开启局面，常用于比赛、棋局、活動或事情的起始階段，也可指整個事務的初期狀態。
explanation_english: Refers to the beginning or opening of an event or situation; commonly used for games, matches, chess openings, or the initial stage of a project or plan.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋而家開局啦，準備好未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 guk6 laa1, zeon2 bei6 hou2 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们现在开局了，准备好了吗？
examples.english_sentence: We're starting the game now — are you ready?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢盤棋嘅開局好緊要，影響整局走勢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 pun4 kei4 ge3 hoi1 guk6 hou2 gan2 jiu3, jing2 hoeng2 zing2 guk6 zau2 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这盘棋的开局很重要，影响整盘的走势。
examples.english_sentence: The opening of this chess game is important; it affects the course of the whole match.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司開局階段需要穩紮穩打，唔好急住擴張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 hoi1 guk6 gaai1 dyun6 seoi1 jiu3 wan2 zaa1 wan2 daa2, m4 hou2 gap1 zyu6 kwaang3 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司在开局阶段需要稳扎稳打，不要急于扩张。
examples.english_sentence: A company in its initial stage should proceed steadily; don't rush to expand.

mandarin_meaning: 开展 (kāizhǎn)
english_meaning: to launch, carry out, develop, or start (an activity, project, plan, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 表示開始推行、展開或發展某項工作、活動、計劃或事務。
explanation_english: To begin, launch, or carry out an activity, project, plan, or operation; to develop or expand something into action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司下個月會開展新項目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 hoi1 zin2 san1 hong6 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司下个月会开展新项目。
examples.english_sentence: The company will launch a new project next month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學校下學期會開展多項課外活動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 haau6 haa6 hok6 kei4 wui5 hoi1 zin2 do1 hong6 fo3 ngoi6 wut6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学校下学期会开展多项课外活动。
examples.english_sentence: The school will carry out multiple extracurricular activities next semester.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府計劃開展一系列復甦措施。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gai3 waak6 hoi1 zin2 jat1 hai6 lit6 fuk6 sou1 cou3 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府计划开展一系列复苏措施。
examples.english_sentence: The government plans to roll out a series of recovery measures.

mandarin_meaning: 开山（首创、开拓；也指开挖山体、动工）
english_meaning: to break ground; to pioneer; inaugural/opening (also to excavate or clear a mountain for construction)
explanation_mandarin: 原义为开凿山地、动工，常用於工程开挖或动土；引申为开创、首创某个领域或项目，表示打破先例、成为先驱。
explanation_english: Originally means to cut into a mountain or begin excavation/groundwork; by extension it means to pioneer or inaugurate something — to break new ground or be the first to do something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個項目係公司嘅開山之作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hong6 muk6 hai6 gung1 si1 ge3 hoi1 saan1 zi1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个项目是公司的开山之作。
examples.english_sentence: This project is the company's inaugural (breakthrough) work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係香港樂隊界嘅開山人物。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 hoeng1 gong2 ngok6 deoi2 gaai3 ge3 hoi1 saan1 jan4 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是香港乐队界的开山人物。
examples.english_sentence: He is a pioneering figure in Hong Kong's band/music scene.

mandarin_meaning: 開山刀 / 比喻開路者、先鋒
english_meaning: machete; (figurative) trailblazer / pioneer; someone who breaks new ground
explanation_mandarin: 1) 指一種大型的砍伐用刀，常用於砍樹、開路。2) 引申為比喻，指在開創、拓荒或帶頭推動某事的人或首個行動。
explanation_english: 1) A large cutting knife (machete) used for cutting vegetation and opening paths. 2) Figuratively, a person or action that pioneers, paves the way, or leads the opening of something new.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係公司入面嘅開山刀，第一個開拓新市場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gung1 si1 jap6 min6 ge3 hoi1 saan1 dou1, dai6 jat1 go3 hoi1 tok3 san1 si5 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是公司裡的開山刀，第一個開拓新市場。
examples.english_sentence: He is the company's trailblazer—the first to open up new markets.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 工人用開山刀砍樹開路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 jan4 jung6 hoi1 saan1 dou1 ham2 syu6 hoi1 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 工人用開山刀砍樹開路。
examples.english_sentence: Workers used a machete to cut trees and clear a path.

mandarin_meaning: 開山祖師（創立者、創始人）
english_meaning: founding master; founder; pioneer
explanation_mandarin: 指創立某一宗派、廟宇、門派或事業的第一代祖師或開創者；也可比喻某一領域的創始者或先驅。
explanation_english: Refers to the founding master who established a temple, sect, school, or enterprise; figuratively used for a founder or pioneer in a field.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間廟嘅開山祖師係一位大師，幾百年前嚟到呢度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 miu6 ge3 hoi1 saan1 zou2 si1 hai6 jat1 wai2 daai6 si1, gei2 baak3 nin4 cin4 lai4 dou3 ni1 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間廟的開山祖師是一位大師，幾百年前來到這裡。
examples.english_sentence: The founding master of this temple was a great master who came here several hundred years ago.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係間公司嘅開山祖師，當年由佢一手創立。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gaan1 gung1 si1 ge3 hoi1 saan1 zou2 si1, dong1 nin4 jau4 keoi5 jat1 sau2 cong3 laap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是這間公司的開山祖師，當年由他一手創立。
examples.english_sentence: He is the company's founder; he founded it single-handedly years ago.

mandarin_meaning: 开工（开始工作、开业、开始施工或恢复工作）
english_meaning: to start work; to commence operations; to begin construction; to resume work
explanation_mandarin: 表示开始工作、开业、开工建设，或在假期/停工后恢复工作。可用于公司、工地或个人上班等情境。
explanation_english: Indicates beginning work, opening for business, starting construction, or resuming work after a break. Used for companies, construction sites, or individuals starting their shift.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋朝早九點開工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ziu1 zou2 gau2 dim2 hoi1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們早上九點開工。
examples.english_sentence: We start work at 9 AM.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 颱風過咗之後工地未開工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: toi4 fung1 gwo3 zo2 zi1 hau6 gung1 dei6 mei6 hoi1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 台风过后工地还没开工。
examples.english_sentence: The construction site hasn't resumed work after the typhoon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司下星期一開工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 haa6 sing1 kei4 jat1 hoi1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司下星期一开工。
examples.english_sentence: The company starts work next Monday.

mandarin_meaning: 打開、疏通小巷或巷道，使其可以通行
english_meaning: to open or clear an alley/lane so that it becomes passable
explanation_mandarin: 指把小巷或巷道中的障礙物移走或開闢通道，使人車可以通行。有時也可引申為開闢某種通路或渠道。
explanation_english: Refers to removing obstacles or opening up a small alley/lane so people and vehicles can pass. It can also be used figuratively to mean creating or opening a path.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 颱風之後，街坊合力開巷，清走樹枝同垃圾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: toi4 fung1 zi1 hau6, gaai1 fong1 hap6 lik6 hoi1 hong6, cing1 zau2 syu6 zi1 tung4 laap6 saap3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 颱風之後，街坊合力開巷，清理樹枝和垃圾。
examples.english_sentence: After the typhoon, neighbors worked together to clear the alley of branches and rubbish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開工前要先開巷，方便物資運送出入。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 gung1 cin4 jiu3 sin1 hoi1 hong6, fong1 bin6 mat6 zi1 wan6 sung3 ceot1 jap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 開工前要先開巷，方便物資運送出入。
examples.english_sentence: Before starting work, they had to open the alley first to facilitate transporting materials in and out.

mandarin_meaning: 開市；開張營業、（股市）開市
english_meaning: to open for business; market opening (e.g. stock market); the start of trading
explanation_mandarin: 「開市」可作動詞，指商店或市場開始營業，或指股市等金融市場開始交易；也可作名詞，意指營業開始的時刻或狀態。
explanation_english: “開市” can be used as a verb meaning to open for business (a shop or market) or for a financial market to begin trading; as a noun it refers to the moment or state of business/market opening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間舖禮拜五開市，大家記得去捧場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 lai5 baai3 ng5 hoi1 si5, daai6 gaa1 gei3 dak1 heoi3 paang2 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間店禮拜五開市，大家記得去捧場。
examples.english_sentence: This shop opens for business on Friday; everyone remember to show support.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 股市一開市，股價就開始大幅波動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 si5 jat1 hoi1 si5, gu2 gaa3 zau6 hoi1 ci2 daai6 fuk1 bo1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 股市一開市，股價就開始大幅波動。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as the stock market opens, stock prices begin to fluctuate widely.

mandarin_meaning: 開始宴席／開始用餐
english_meaning: to start a banquet; to begin the meal
explanation_mandarin: 表示宴會或酒席正式開始用餐，常用於婚宴、酒席或正式聚餐場合。
explanation_english: Indicates the formal start of a banquet or meal; commonly used at weddings, banquets, or formal dining events.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 婚禮準備好喇，可以開席喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fan1 lai5 zeon2 bei6 hou2 laa3, ho2 ji5 hoi1 zik6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 婚礼准备好了，可以开席了。
examples.english_sentence: The wedding is ready; we can start the banquet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成枱人都到齊，可以開席喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 toi2 jan4 dou1 dou3 cai4, ho2 ji5 hoi1 zik6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 整桌人都到齐了，可以开席了。
examples.english_sentence: Everyone at the table has arrived; we can start eating.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 司儀話十點鐘正式開席，請各位就座。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 ji4 waa6 sap6 dim2 zung1 zing3 sik1 hoi1 zik6, ceng2 gok3 wai2 zau6 zo6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 司仪说十点钟正式开席，请各位就座。
examples.english_sentence: The MC says the banquet will formally start at 10 o'clock; please take your seats.

mandarin_meaning: 开幕（举行开幕仪式）；开张
english_meaning: to open (an event); opening (ceremony); inaugural
explanation_mandarin: 指活動或展覽正式開始，或舉行開幕典禮。也可指商店等開張。
explanation_english: Refers to the formal beginning of an event or exhibition, often accompanied by an opening ceremony. Can also mean a business opening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日係酒店嘅開幕，我哋要去參加。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 hai6 zau2 dim3 ge3 hoi1 mok6, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 heoi3 caam1 gaa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天是酒店的開幕，我們要去參加。
examples.english_sentence: Tomorrow is the hotel's opening; we will go to attend.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢場展覽嘅開幕式好隆重。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 coeng4 zin2 laam5 ge3 hoi1 mok6 sik1 hou2 lung4 zung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這場展覽的開幕式很隆重。
examples.english_sentence: The opening ceremony of this exhibition is very grand.

mandarin_meaning: 开平（中國廣東省的縣級市）
english_meaning: Kaiping (a county-level city in Guangdong Province, China)
explanation_mandarin: 開平是中國廣東省江門市下轄的一個縣級市，以碉樓（開平碉樓）和僑鄉文化聞名，為世界遺產地之一。
explanation_english: Kaiping is a county-level city in Guangdong Province, China, noted for its diaolou (watchtowers) and overseas Chinese culture; some of its diaolou are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我下個禮拜會去開平旅行。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 wui5 heoi3 hoi1 ping4 leoi5 hang4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我下个礼拜会去开平旅行。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to Kaiping next week.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開平嘅碉樓好有名，吸引好多遊客。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 ping4 ge3 diu1 lau4 hou2 jau5 ming4, hap1 jan5 hou2 do1 jau4 haak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开平的碉楼很有名，吸引很多游客。
examples.english_sentence: Kaiping's diaolou are very famous and attract many tourists.

mandarin_meaning: 開平粽子（廣東開平的地方粽）
english_meaning: Kaiping zongzi (Kaiping-style rice dumpling)
explanation_mandarin: 指源自廣東開平一帶的粽子，屬於地方傳統食物，通常有鹹、甜或肉餡等不同款式，是當地或旅遊時常見的特色小吃。
explanation_english: Refers to a type of zongzi (rice dumpling) originating from Kaiping in Guangdong. It is a local traditional food, available in savory or sweet versions with various fillings, and is a regional specialty often enjoyed by locals and visitors.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝喺街市買咗幾個開平粽，啲肉好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 hai2 gaai1 si5 maai5 zo2 gei2 go3 hoi1 ping4 zung2, di1 juk6 hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上在菜市場買了幾個開平粽，肉很好吃／很香。
examples.english_sentence: This morning I bought several Kaiping zongzi at the market; the meat smelled great.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 去開平旅行唔可以唔試開平粽，係當地嘅特色小吃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: heoi3 hoi1 ping4 leoi5 hang4 m4 ho2 ji5 m4 si3 hoi1 ping4 zung2, hai6 dong1 dei6 ge3 dak6 sik1 siu2 hek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去開平旅行一定要嘗試開平粽，它是當地的特色小吃。
examples.english_sentence: When traveling to Kaiping you must try Kaiping zongzi; it's a local specialty snack.

mandarin_meaning: 开平粽（开平地区的传统粽子）
english_meaning: Kaiping zongzi (a type of rice dumpling from Kaiping, Guangdong)
explanation_mandarin: 開平糭是廣東開平地區的傳統粽子，通常以糯米為主，內餡常見有五花肉、鹹蛋黃、香菇、花生等，口味偏鹹香且帶有地方風味，包法與調味有其特色，為當地及周邊地區的節慶和日常小吃之一。
explanation_english: Kaiping zongzi is a traditional rice dumpling from Kaiping in Guangdong. It is made with glutinous rice and typically contains fillings such as pork belly, salted egg yolk, shiitake mushrooms, and peanuts. The flavor is savory and fragrant with regional seasoning and wrapping methods, and it is a local festive and everyday snack.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間舖嘅開平糭好出名，成日有人排隊買。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 ge3 hoi1 ping4 zung2 hou2 ceot1 ming4, sing4 jat6 jau5 jan4 paai4 deoi6 maai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间店的开平粽很出名，总是有人排队购买。
examples.english_sentence: This shop's Kaiping zongzi are famous; people often line up to buy them.

mandarin_meaning: 开年（年初；新年开始）
english_meaning: start of the year; the beginning of the year; to kick off the year
explanation_mandarin: 指新一年的開始，常用來描述年初的時候或在年初舉行或發生的活動（如開年拜年、開年做生意等）。在廣東話中為口語常用語，尤見於香港用法。
explanation_english: Refers to the start of the year; used to describe the early period of the year or activities that kick off the year (e.g. New Year visits, first business of the year). Common colloquial Cantonese usage, especially in Hong Kong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開年大家都會去親戚屋企拜年。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 nin4 daai6 gaa1 dou1 wui5 heoi3 can1 cik1 uk1 kei2 baai3 nin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开年大家都会去亲戚家拜年。
examples.english_sentence: At the start of the year, everyone goes to relatives' homes to pay New Year visits.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋開年第一單生意做得幾好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hoi1 nin4 dai6 jat1 daan1 saang1 ji3 zou6 dak1 gei2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们开年第一单生意做得挺好。
examples.english_sentence: We did pretty well on the first deal of the year.

mandarin_meaning: 开年饭；新年之始与家人、朋友或同事聚餐庆祝新年
english_meaning: New Year (opening) meal — the first meal or celebratory meal at the start of the Lunar New Year, often with family, friends, or colleagues
explanation_mandarin: 指農曆新年期間或年初舉行的聚餐，既可指家人團聚的飯，也可指公司或朋友在年初舉行的慶祝飯局或開工飯。
explanation_english: Refers to a meal held at the start of the Lunar New Year — can mean a family reunion meal or a celebratory gathering (including company kick‑off or colleagues' meal) marking the new year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年我哋一家打算喺年初一食開年飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 ngo5 dei6 jat1 gaa1 daa2 syun3 hai2 nin4 co1 jat1 sik6 hoi1 nin4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年我们一家打算在年初一吃开年饭。
examples.english_sentence: This year my family plans to have the opening New Year meal on the first day of the lunar year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司嘅開年飯會喺下星期五喺酒樓舉行。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ge3 hoi1 nin4 faan6 wui5 hai2 haa6 sing1 kei4 ng5 hai2 zau2 lau4 geoi2 hang4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的开年饭会在下星期五在酒楼举行。
examples.english_sentence: The company's New Year banquet will be held at a restaurant next Friday.

mandarin_meaning: 洞房 / 發生性行為
english_meaning: to consummate (a marriage); to sleep with someone / have sexual relations
explanation_mandarin: 通常指新婚夫婦在婚禮後第一次同床共枕、完成夫妻生活；口語中也泛指與某人發生性關係。
explanation_english: Usually refers to a newlywed couple consummating their marriage (first night together); colloquially it can mean having sexual relations with someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋禮拜五舉行咗婚禮，昨晚先開床。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 lai5 baai3 ng5 geoi2 hang4 zo2 fan1 lai5, zok6 maan5 sin1 hoi1 cong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们星期五举办了婚礼，昨晚才洞房。
examples.english_sentence: They held their wedding on Friday and only consummated the marriage last night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你哋認識咁短嘅時間就開床？唔好咁衝動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 jing6 sik1 gam2 dyun2 ge3 si4 gaan3 zau6 hoi1 cong4? m4 hou2 gam2 cung1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你们认识这么短的时间就发生性关系？别这么冲动。
examples.english_sentence: You two have sex after knowing each other for such a short time? Don't be so impulsive.

mandarin_meaning: （婚禮習俗）舉行開床（鋪婚床、啟用洞房）的儀式；（口語/婉轉）指夫妻或情侶發生性關係、洞房
english_meaning: Literally 'open the bed' — in wedding customs, to prepare/unveil the marital bed; colloquially/euphemistically, to have sex or consummate a marriage.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞短語 / 名詞（視語境而定，含習俗與婉轉用法）
partOfSpeech_english: verb phrase (ceremonial or euphemistic); noun in ceremonial context
explanation_mandarin: 「開床」在廣東話一方面指婚禮中鋪設或啟用洞房的傳統儀式；另一方面常作婉轉或俚語，指夫妻或情侶發生性關係（相當於「洞房」或「上床」）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開床' can refer to the traditional wedding ritual of preparing or unveiling the bridal bed. It is also used euphemistically or as slang to mean having sex or consummating a marriage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 結婚果日，阿媽叫埋啲親戚嚟幫手開床。
examples.jyutping_sentence: git3 fan1 go2 jat6, aa3 maa1 giu3 maai4 di1 can1 cik1 lai4 bong1 sau2 hoi1 cong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 結婚那天，媽媽叫親戚來幫忙開床。
examples.english_sentence: On the wedding day, Mom had relatives come to help 'open' the marital bed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你哋今晚會唔會開床？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 gam1 maan5 wui5 m4 wui5 hoi1 cong4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你們今晚會不會開床？（婉轉指發生性關係）
examples.english_sentence: Are you two going to 'open the bed' tonight? (euphemism for having sex/consummating)

mandarin_meaning: 開帳；先墊錢／先放一筆（作為賭注、買單或開台等）
english_meaning: to open a tab / to put down an initial stake or deposit (e.g. for a bet, a tab, or to start a session)
explanation_mandarin: 在口語（常見於香港）中，『開底』指先墊出一筆錢或開一個帳目，作為賭注、買單或開台（例如卡拉OK／麻將）等的起始款項。有時也指店家或朋友先幫忙記帳或代墊。
explanation_english: Colloquial (commonly used in Hong Kong). '開底' means to put down an initial sum or open an account/tab—used for an initial stake in gambling, opening a tab/bill, or fronting money to start a session (e.g., karaoke, mahjong). It can also mean someone fronts payment or allows a charge to be put on account.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去卡拉OK，阿明話佢請，唔使我哋開底。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 kaa1 laa1 O1, aa3 ming4 waa6 keoi5 cing2, m4 sai2 ngo5 dei6 hoi1 dai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去卡拉OK，阿明說他請，不用我們先墊錢／開帳。
examples.english_sentence: We're going to karaoke tonight. Ming said he'll pay, so we don't need to open a tab.

mandarin_meaning: 开庭
english_meaning: to open a court session; to hold a trial/hearing
explanation_mandarin: 在法院开始审理案件、举行法庭程序。
explanation_english: To begin a court session; to hold a trial or hearing in a court.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 法庭下星期一會開庭審理呢宗案件。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 ting4 haa6 sing1 kei4 jat1 wui5 hoi1 ting4 sam2 lei5 ni1 zung1 on3 gin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 法院将在下星期一开庭审理这宗案件。
examples.english_sentence: The court will hold a hearing for this case next Monday.

mandarin_meaning: 打引号；在话语前后加引号（可表示引用、讽刺或保留态度）
english_meaning: to put in quotation marks; to quote; to use 'air quotes' (to indicate irony, skepticism, or distance)
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，「開引號」是口語用法，字面意思是「打開引號/加引號」。可用來表示直接引用某人的話，也常用來用引號標示諷刺、懷疑或與所述保持距離，類似英語的 air quotes。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "開引號" is a colloquial expression literally meaning "open quotation marks." It can mean to quote someone directly, or to put words in quotes to signal irony, skepticism, or to distance oneself from the statement (similar to English "air quotes").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開引號話：「呢件事唔關我事」，其實係想推卸責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 jan5 hou6 waa6: 'ni1 gin6 si6 m4 gwaan1 ngo5 si6', kei4 sat6 hai6 soeng2 teoi1 se6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打引号说：「这件事跟我无关」，其实是在推卸责任。
examples.english_sentence: He put it in quotes and said, "This has nothing to do with me," but actually he was trying to shirk responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 報導用「專家」去形容佢，開引號暗示有保留。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou3 dou6 jung6 'zyun1 gaa1' heoi3 jing4 joeng4 keoi5, hoi1 jan5 hou6 aam3 si6 jau5 bou2 lau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 报道用「专家」来形容他，打引号暗示有所保留。
examples.english_sentence: The report described him as an "expert"; putting it in quotes suggests some reservation.

mandarin_meaning: 开张（开始营业）
english_meaning: to open (a shop/business); to begin operations; grand opening
explanation_mandarin: 表示商店或生意開始營業，或舉行開業、開幕的意思，也可指生意開始運作。
explanation_english: Refers to a shop or business starting operations or holding a grand opening; to begin business activity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋下星期要開張，希望生意興隆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 haa6 sing1 kei4 jiu3 hoi1 zoeng1, hei1 mong6 saang1 ji3 hing1 lung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們下星期要開張，希望生意興隆。
examples.english_sentence: We're opening next week; hope business will be prosperous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新店今晚正式開張，大家記得嚟支持。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 dim3 gam1 maan5 zing3 sik1 hoi1 zoeng1, daai6 gaa1 gei3 dak1 lai4 zi1 ci4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新店今晚正式開張，大家記得來支持。
examples.english_sentence: The new shop officially opens tonight; everyone remember to come and support it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋為咗開張，已經做好晒宣傳同準備工作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 wai6 zo2 hoi1 zoeng1, ji5 ging1 zou6 hou2 saai3 syun1 cyun4 tung4 zeon2 bei6 gung1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們為了開張，已經做好了宣傳和準備工作。
examples.english_sentence: They've already finished publicity and preparations for the opening.

mandarin_meaning: 開獎；揭示彩票或賭博的結果
english_meaning: to draw/announce the results of a lottery or betting game; to announce the winning numbers
explanation_mandarin: 「開彩」常用於賭博或彩票語境，指公布或揭示中獎號碼、賭局結果，等同於「開獎」。
explanation_english: Commonly used in gambling or lottery contexts to mean announcing or revealing the winning numbers or outcomes of a bet; equivalent to 'draw the lottery' or 'announce results'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚六合彩幾點開彩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 luk6 hap6 coi2 gei2 dim2 hoi1 coi2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚六合彩幾點開獎？
examples.english_sentence: What time will the Mark Six lottery be drawn tonight?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等陣開彩先睇到我哋中唔中獎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 zan6 hoi1 coi2 sin1 tai2 dou3 ngo5 dei6 zung1 m4 zung6 zoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等一下開獎才能看到我們有沒有中獎。
examples.english_sentence: Wait until the draw to see whether we won.

mandarin_meaning: 开心 (kāixīn)
english_meaning: happy; joyful; pleased
explanation_mandarin: 表示心情愉快、满足或高兴，用来形容人的情绪状态。
explanation_english: Expresses a feeling of happiness, pleasure, or joy; used to describe someone's emotional state.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1jat6 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天很开心。
examples.english_sentence: I'm very happy today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到呢個消息我好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 ni1 go3 siu1sik1 ngo5 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听到这个消息我很开心。
examples.english_sentence: I was very happy to hear this news.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 同朋友一齊食飯真係好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tung4 pang4jau5 jat1 cai4 sik6 faan6 zan1 hai6 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 和朋友一起吃饭真的很开心。
examples.english_sentence: It's really nice/I'm really happy to eat with friends.

mandarin_meaning: 開心一點吧 / 高興一點吧
english_meaning: Cheer up a bit; be a little happier
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語表達，用來勸人放鬆心情、開心一點。當中「些牙」相當於常見的「啲呀／一點吧」，是語氣詞的變體，帶有輕鬆或催促的語氣。
explanation_english: An informal Cantonese expression used to tell someone to be a little happier or to cheer up. The segment "些牙" functions like the colloquial "啲呀" (a bit, come on) and serves as a softening/exhortative particle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁唔開心，開心些牙啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 m4 hoi1 sam1, hoi1 sam1 se1 ngaa4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要那麼不開心，開心一點吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so unhappy — cheer up a bit.

synonyms: 開心啲呀 (hoi1 sam1 di1 aa3)
高興啲啦 (gou1 hing3 di1 laa1)

mandarin_meaning: 开心果（坚果）；比喻能使人开心、活跃气氛的人
english_meaning: pistachio; (colloquial) a person who cheers others up, the 'life of the party'
explanation_mandarin: 1) 指一种常见的坚果，即开心果。2) 引申为比喻用法，指性格开朗、能逗人发笑、带动气氛的人。
explanation_english: 1) A type of nut (pistachio). 2) Figuratively, a person who makes others happy or livens up a group; the life of the party.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我鍾意食開心果，佢好香好脆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 ji3 sik6 hoi1 sam1 gwo2, keoi5 hou2 hoeng1 hou2 ceoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我喜欢吃开心果，它很香很脆。
examples.english_sentence: I like eating pistachios; they're fragrant and crunchy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿明係我哋班嘅開心果，成日講笑，帶動晒氣氛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ming4 hai6 ngo5 dei6 baan1 ge3 hoi1 sam1 gwo2, sing4 jat6 gong2 siu3, daai3 dung6 saai3 hei3 fan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿明是我们班的开心果，经常说笑，带动了气氛。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Ming is the life of our class; he jokes all the time and livens up the atmosphere.

mandarin_meaning: 坦誠相見；開誠布公，敞開心胸、真誠相待
english_meaning: to be open and sincere; to speak frankly and honestly
explanation_mandarin: 表示敞開心扉、真誠相對，常用於勸人說話或處事要坦率。
explanation_english: An idiomatic expression meaning to be open-hearted and sincere; used to urge frank and honest communication or behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋開會嘅時候，大家要開心見誠，唔好驚講真心話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hoi1 wui6 ge3 si4 hau6, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 hoi1 sam1 gin3 sing4, m4 hou2 ging1 gong2 zan1 sam1 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們開會的時候，大家要坦誠相見，不要害怕說真心話。
examples.english_sentence: When we have the meeting, everyone should be open and honest; don't be afraid to speak your mind.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對客戶好開心見誠，所以生意做得更好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 haak3 wu6 hou2 hoi1 sam1 gin3 sing4, so2 ji5 saang1 ji3 zou6 dak1 gang3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對客戶很坦誠，所以生意做得更好。
examples.english_sentence: He was very open and sincere with the clients, so the business did better.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）開車超速；（口語）匆忙行事或加快進度
english_meaning: to speed (drive fast); colloquially, to rush or speed up a process
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指開車時超速行駛；在口語中也常用來比喻做事匆忙、趕工或加快進度。該詞在香港廣東話中較常見。
explanation_english: Literally means to drive at high speed. Colloquially used to describe doing something hastily, rushing a job, or accelerating progress. Common in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺條馬路上開快車，好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 tiu4 maa5 lou6 soeng6 hoi1 faai3 ce1, hou2 ngai4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在馬路上超速開車，真危險。
examples.english_sentence: He's speeding on the road; it's really dangerous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司唔好再開快車，做事情要穩陣啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 m4 hou2 zoi3 hoi1 faai3 ce1, zou6 si6 cing4 jiu3 wan2 zan6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司不要再匆忙行事，做事要穩妥一點。
examples.english_sentence: The company shouldn't rush things anymore; work should be more steady.

mandarin_meaning: 开怀；高兴、心情舒畅；畅快地笑或尽情地做某事
english_meaning: to be open-hearted; to feel cheerful or joyful; to laugh heartily or be in high spirits
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容词/动词（视语境而定）
explanation_mandarin: “開懷”表示心情开朗、愉快，有时也指畅快地笑或尽情享受。可作形容词或动词短语使用。
explanation_english: “開懷” describes being cheerful or in high spirits; it can also mean to laugh heartily or enjoy oneself freely. It functions as an adjective or a verb phrase depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚飲得開懷啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 jam2 dak1 hoi1 waai4 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚喝得很开心！
examples.english_sentence: We drank heartily tonight! / We had a great time drinking tonight!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅笑容令我開懷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 siu3 jung4 ling6 ngo5 hoi1 waai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的笑容让我开怀。
examples.english_sentence: His smile made me feel cheerful.

mandarin_meaning: 開戰 (kāizhàn)
english_meaning: to go to war; to start a battle or hostilities; to begin a fight (can be literal or figurative)
explanation_mandarin: 表示開始戰爭或發動攻擊，也可用於比喻性的衝突或爭執（例如網上或口頭的激烈爭論）。
explanation_english: Indicates the start of a war or the launching of an attack; can also be used figuratively for a conflict, confrontation, or heated dispute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩國終於開戰喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 gwok3 zung1 jyu1 hoi1 zin3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 兩國終於開戰了。
examples.english_sentence: The two countries have finally gone to war.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果佢哋再攻擊我哋，我哋就會開戰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 keoi5 dei6 zoi3 gung1 gik1 ngo5 dei6, ngo5 dei6 zau6 wui5 hoi1 zin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果他們再攻擊我們，我們就會開戰。
examples.english_sentence: If they attack us again, we'll go to war.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩隊球迷喺網上開戰，留言多到爆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 deoi6 kau4 mai4 hai2 mong5 soeng6 hoi1 zin3, lau4 jin4 do1 dou3 baau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 兩隊球迷在網上開戰，留言多到爆。
examples.english_sentence: Fans of the two teams started fighting online; the comments exploded.

mandarin_meaning: 開始演出／開場；（口語）做戲、裝腔作勢、鬧事
english_meaning: to start a show or screening; (colloquial) to put on an act, make a scene
explanation_mandarin: 「開戲」在廣東話可指戲劇、電影等開始演出或放映（例如戲院開戲）。口語用法還可表示「做戲」或「演戲」，含故意表演、裝模作樣或鬧事的意思。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開戲' literally means to start a performance or screening (e.g. a movie/theatre begins). Colloquially it can also mean to put on an act, make a scene, or stage a dramatic display.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 戲院五點鐘開戲，你幾點到？
examples.jyutping_sentence: hei3 jyun2 ng5 dim2 zung1 hoi1 hei3, nei5 gei2 dim2 dou3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 戲院五點鐘開演，你幾點到？
examples.english_sentence: The theater starts at five o'clock. What time will you arrive?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺度開戲，想引人注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 dou6 hoi1 hei3, soeng2 jan5 jan4 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在那裡做戲，想引人注意。
examples.english_sentence: He's putting on an act there, trying to attract attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 記者會準時兩點開戲，記得唔好遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gei3 ze2 wui2 zeon2 si4 loeng5 dim2 hoi1 hei3, gei3 dak1 m4 hou2 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 記者會準時兩點開始，記得不要遲到。
examples.english_sentence: The press conference starts at two on time—remember not to be late.

mandarin_meaning: 开户
english_meaning: to open an account (e.g., bank account)
explanation_mandarin: 在銀行或其他金融機構開立帳戶，通常指開設銀行帳戶或相關服務賬戶。
explanation_english: To open an account at a bank or other financial institution, typically referring to setting up a bank account or related service account.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我要去銀行開戶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jiu3 heoi3 ngan4 hong4 hoi1 wu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我要去银行开户。
examples.english_sentence: I need to go to the bank to open an account.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開戶要帶身份證同填表格。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 wu6 jiu3 daai3 san1 fan6 zing3 tung4 tin4 biu2 gaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开户要带身份证并填写表格。
examples.english_sentence: To open an account you need to bring your ID and fill out forms.

mandarin_meaning: 开户（在银行或机构开立账户）
english_meaning: to open an (bank or service) account; to register an account
explanation_mandarin: 指在銀行、證券公司或網絡平台等處開設帳戶或註冊賬號，通常需要提供個人資料與證件。
explanation_english: Refers to opening an account at a bank, brokerage, or online platform; usually involves providing personal information and identification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我打算下星期去銀行開户。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 daa2 syun3 haa6 sing1 kei4 heoi3 ngan4 hong4 hoi1 wu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我打算下星期去银行开户。
examples.english_sentence: I'm planning to go to the bank next week to open an account.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家好多服務都可以網上開户，好方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 hou2 do1 fuk6 mou6 dou1 ho2 ji5 mong5 soeng5 hoi1 wu6, hou2 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在很多服务都可以网上开户，很方便。
examples.english_sentence: Nowadays many services let you open accounts online; it's very convenient.

mandarin_meaning: 开房（在酒店订房；常作委婉语指在酒店发生性关系）
english_meaning: to book/rent a hotel room; often used euphemistically to imply having sex in a hotel
explanation_mandarin: 口语/俚语，指在酒店开房间。根据语境可为中性（订房、留宿）或委婉指发生性行为。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to book or rent a hotel room. Depending on context it can be neutral (booking/staying overnight) or a euphemism for having sexual relations in a hotel.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚要開房，因為聽日有早機，唔想趕返屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 hoi1 fong2, jan1 wai6 ting1 jat6 jau5 zou2 gei1, m4 soeng2 gan2 faan1 uk1 kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚要开房，因为明天一早有飞机，不想赶回家。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to book a hotel room tonight because I have an early flight tomorrow and don't want to rush back home.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋見面之後就去開房，唔想畀人知。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gin3 min6 zi1 hau6 zau6 heoi3 hoi1 fong2, m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们见面之后就去开房，不想让别人知道。
examples.english_sentence: They went to book a room after meeting up; they didn't want others to know.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「開房」喺廣東話有時係委婉講法，指去酒店發生性關係。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 'hoi1 fong2' hai2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2 jau5 si4 hai6 wai2 waan2 gong2 faat3, zi2 heoi3 zau2 dim3 faat3 sang1 sing3 gwaan1 hai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: “开房”在广东话有时是委婉说法，指去酒店发生性关系。
examples.english_sentence: '開房' in Cantonese is sometimes a euphemism referring to having sexual relations in a hotel.

mandarin_meaning: 開始；出手（著手）或張開手
english_meaning: to start/begin (an action); to take the first move; to open one's hand
explanation_mandarin: 「開手」在廣東話常用作動詞，表示開始做某事、著手處理或先出手幫忙；在字面上也可指張開手。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "開手" is commonly used as a verb meaning to start/begin an action, to take the initiative (make the first move), or to begin helping; literally it can also mean to open one's hand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋宜家開手做功課啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 sau2 zou6 gung1 fo3 laa1
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們現在開始做功課吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's start doing our homework now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一見到機會就開手幫忙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gin3 dou3 gei1 wui6 zau6 hoi1 sau2 bong1 mong4
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一看到機會就出手幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: He jumps in to help as soon as he sees an opportunity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好隨便開手，可能會惹事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seoi4 bin6 hoi1 sau2, ho2 nang4 wui5 je5 si6
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要隨便動手，可能會惹事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't start acting/get physical carelessly; it might cause trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 開始投票 / 投票已經開始
english_meaning: to start voting; (the polls) are open
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用法，表示「開始投票」或「投票已經開始」，常用於選舉、民調或投票活動中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning 'to start voting' or 'the voting has begun' (i.e. the polls are open). Commonly used for elections, polls, or voting events.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 選舉而家開投，大家快啲去投票啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: syun2 geoi2 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 tau4, daai6 gaa1 faai3 di1 heoi3 tau4 piu3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 選舉現在開始投票了，大家快去投票吧。
examples.english_sentence: The election voting has started; everyone hurry to vote.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個民調已經開投，投票嘅時間仲有三日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 man4 diu6 ji5 ging1 hoi1 tau4, tau4 piu3 ge3 si4 gaan3 zung6 jau5 saam1 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個民調已經開始投票，投票的時間還有三天。
examples.english_sentence: This poll has opened for voting; there are still three days left to vote.

mandarin_meaning: 开拍（kāi pāi）；开始拍摄
english_meaning: to start filming/shooting (a movie, TV show, commercial); to begin recording
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指電影、電視劇或廣告等開始進行拍攝；有時也泛指某件事正式開始。
explanation_english: Colloquial phrase meaning to begin filming (a movie, TV show, commercial, etc.). It can also be used more generally to mean something officially starts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電影終於開拍喇，大家準備好未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 jing2 zung1 jyu1 hoi1 paak3 laa3, daai6 gaa1 zeon2 bei6 hou2 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 电影终于开拍了，大家准备好了吗？
examples.english_sentence: The movie is finally starting filming — is everyone ready?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 導演話下星期會開拍部新劇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dou6 jin2 waa6 haa6 sing1 kei4 wui5 hoi1 paak3 bou6 san1 kek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 导演说下星期会开拍一部新剧。
examples.english_sentence: The director said the new drama will start shooting next week.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個廣告下星期一開拍，要趁早排期。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 gwong2 gou3 haa6 sing1 kei4 jat1 hoi1 paak3, jiu3 can3 zou2 paai4 kei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个广告下星期一开拍，要趁早排期。
examples.english_sentence: That commercial starts shooting next Monday; schedule it early.

mandarin_meaning: 开拓（开发、拓展新的领域、地区或市场）
english_meaning: to open up; to develop; to pioneer or expand into new areas, territories, or markets
explanation_mandarin: 「開拓」指開發、開墾或拓展新的領域、地區或市場，既可用於土地開墾，也可用於市場、視野等抽象範疇的擴展。
